default.title: Welcome to Temari
default.intro: Start with the basics — how school & branch views and navigation work:

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.tagline: School & branch views, navigation and the basics

dashboard.title: Read your dashboard
dashboard.summary: The dashboard is your command center: it shows today's vitals, the work waiting for your decision, and your day — shaped by your role.
dashboard.step1: The top strip shows today's Ethiopian date and, in a branch view, the running semester with its week number and days left.
dashboard.step2: The vitals tiles answer the morning questions at a glance: students enrolled, attendance today, money collected this month, outstanding fees and staff present. Tap any tile to open its module.
dashboard.step3: "Needs your attention" lists the piles waiting on you — enrollments to activate, payments to verify, leave and expenses to decide, marklists to approve. Tap a card to go decide.
dashboard.step4: Teachers see "My day": today's classes from the published timetable with a live marker, homerooms still to mark with a one-tap Take attendance button, and work piles like submissions to grade.
dashboard.step5: Below, the charts show the last week's attendance, six months of collections, and who studies here. School managers in the All-branches view also get a per-branch comparison.
dashboard.tip: Everything on the dashboard respects your role and selected school or branch — if a block is missing, your role simply doesn't cover it. Numbers refresh every few minutes.

workspace.title: Choose where you're working
workspace.summary: Everything in Temari is scoped to a school & branch view. The school/branch switcher decides whose data you see and act on.
workspace.step1: Open the school/branch switcher at the top of the sidebar (top bar on mobile).
workspace.step2: Pick the school, then the branch you want to work in.
workspace.step3: Everything you now see — students, employees, fees — belongs to that branch only.
workspace.step4: Your menu changes with the selected school or branch: you only see what your role there allows.
workspace.tip: School managers can stay in the school-wide (All branches) view: lists show every branch, and create forms simply ask which branch the record belongs to. Branch employees pick their branch in the switcher.

navigation.title: Find your way around
navigation.summary: The app is organized into a few areas; you only see the ones your role can use.
navigation.step1: On a computer, the left sidebar groups everything into Organization, Academic, People and Operations.
navigation.step2: On a phone, your most-used areas sit in the bottom tab bar; everything else is under Menu.
navigation.step3: A shorter menu than a colleague's is normal — it reflects your role, not a problem.
navigation.step4: Every list has search, filters, sorting and export built in — start typing in the search box above any table.

globalSearch.title: Search everything at once
globalSearch.summary: The search box (⌘K or Ctrl+K anywhere) finds students, employees, parents, sections, invoices, payments and LMS content (exams, assignments, courses, materials) across your whole workspace in one place.
globalSearch.step1: Press ⌘K (Mac) or Ctrl+K (Windows), or tap the search box at the top of the sidebar.
globalSearch.step2: Type anything you know — a name (in any order, e.g. "abebe kebede"), a phone number (with or without dashes), an email, an ID code like H8R6WV, an invoice number, a receipt number (RCT-…), a bank reference from a receipt, or the title of an exam, assignment or course.
globalSearch.step3: Results are grouped: pick a student to open their profile, an invoice to land on the student's fees tab, a page name to jump straight there.
globalSearch.step4: Small typos are okay — "Abeba" still finds "Abebe". Your most recent picks appear when you open search again.
globalSearch.tip: You only ever see people from your own school & branch view — search obeys the same permissions as every list.

attachFiles.title: Attach a file
attachFiles.summary: Every place that takes a file works the same way: pick it, name it, send it — and on a computer you can simply drag it in.
attachFiles.step1: Press the attach button (paperclip) wherever you see it — a student's Documents tab, a message, an assignment, a transfer request.
attachFiles.step2: On a computer you can skip the button: drag the file from your desktop onto the area and drop it. A dashed outline shows where it will land.
attachFiles.step3: Give the file a clear name before it is sent — "Birth certificate" reads better than IMG_2431. The file type is kept for you.
attachFiles.step4: Files of the wrong type, or bigger than the limit, are refused straight away and say why — nothing is sent silently.
attachFiles.tip: Dropping a photo on someone's picture changes their photo; dropping a document on the Documents area files it. Aim for the area you mean.

sortTables.title: Sort any table
sortTables.summary: Every list — students, employees, results, fees — can be re-ordered by any column, so the rows you need rise to the top.
sortTables.step1: Open any list page, for example Students or Employees.
sortTables.step2: Click a column header to sort by that field — an arrow next to the header shows the current order.
sortTables.step3: Click the same header again to flip between ascending and descending.
sortTables.step4: On a phone, tap the Sort pill in the table toolbar, choose a field, and tap it again to flip the direction.
sortTables.tip: Numbers and dates sort by value, not letter by letter, and empty cells always sink to the bottom — the useful rows stay on top.

bulkRows.title: Do the same thing to many rows at once
bulkRows.summary: Most tables let you tick several rows and act on the whole selection from one bar.
bulkRows.step1: Tick the box on each row you want. On a phone, tap Select first, then tap the rows.
bulkRows.step2: A dark bar appears at the bottom of the screen with the count and everything you can do to that selection.
bulkRows.step3: You only ever see actions you are allowed to perform — the bar mirrors the buttons on a single row.
bulkRows.step4: Confirm when asked. Approvals and rejections ask for a note first; a rejection always needs one.
bulkRows.step5: You are told how many succeeded. If any row was skipped, a second message names it and says why — nothing is ever silently left out.
bulkRows.tip: Rows outside your school or branch, rows already decided, and your own account are always skipped, so a wide selection is safe. Filter or search first, then tick the box in the header to select the whole page.

pageSize.title: Show more rows at once
pageSize.summary: Long lists arrive 25 rows at a time. Change that to 50, 75 or 100 whenever you want to see more in one go.
pageSize.step1: Scroll to the bottom of any long list. On the left of the footer sits a small button showing the current number — for example 25.
pageSize.step2: Tap it and choose 25, 50, 75 or 100 rows.
pageSize.step3: The list reloads from the top of the page, and the count beside the button always tells you which rows you are looking at — for example "1–100 of 320".
pageSize.step4: Your choice is remembered for every list on this device — set it once and every register opens the way you like it.
pageSize.tip: Short lists have no page control at all: if everything already fits on one page, there is nothing to page through. On a slow connection keep 25 — fewer rows load faster.

emptyDropdowns.title: When a dropdown has nothing to pick
emptyDropdowns.summary: An empty dropdown is never a dead end — instead of a blank list it tells you which setup step is missing.
emptyDropdowns.step1: Open the dropdown as usual. Instead of a blank list you see a short note explaining why it is empty.
emptyDropdowns.step2: The note names the missing step — for example "No active semester — activate one first" or "No branches yet — add a branch first".
emptyDropdowns.step3: Complete that setup step (or ask the manager responsible for it), then come back — the options appear automatically.
emptyDropdowns.tip: Typical prerequisites: a branch, an active academic year and semester, the branch's grade offering, and sections under the grade.

language.title: Language & theme
language.summary: Temari speaks English, Amharic and Afaan Oromoo, in light or dark.
language.step1: Click your name at the bottom of the sidebar (or open the mobile menu) and pick English, አማርኛ or Afaan Oromoo.
language.step2: Your choice is saved to your account and follows you on any device.
language.step3: Use the theme toggle next to it to switch between light and dark.
language.tip: Changing language only changes the interface — your school's data stays exactly as it was entered.

calendarClock.title: Ethiopian calendar & time
calendarClock.summary: The app writes dates the way your school does — in the Ethiopian calendar (Hamle 15, 2018) or the Gregorian one (July 22, 2026), and times as standard (8:00 AM) or Ethiopian time (2:00 in the morning).
calendarClock.step1: Your school chooses the calendar and time style once, in School settings → Academic. Every date and time in the app, in SMS messages and in reports then follows it.
calendarClock.step2: A branch that works differently can set its own choice in Branch settings — it wins over the school's.
calendarClock.step3: When picking a date, the calendar shows Ethiopian months (Meskerem to Pagume) or Gregorian months to match the setting — either way the record saved is the same.
calendarClock.tip: Official papers — receipts, transcripts, letters — always print BOTH dates, so they are understood anywhere.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.summary: The bell keeps you on top of payments, attendance, approvals and school work.
notifications.step1: Watch the bell (top of the sidebar on desktop, top-right on mobile). A red badge counts what you have not read yet.
notifications.step2: Tap a notification to jump straight to the thing it talks about — an invoice, an approval, an assignment.
notifications.step3: Open the full feed to filter by topic (fees, attendance, approvals…) or show only unread.
notifications.step4: In Settings you can mute topics per channel (SMS, email). In-app notifications are always on.
notifications.tip: Critical alerts — a new sign-in to your account, money due, your child absent — are always delivered, even if a topic is muted.

schools.title: Schools & branches
schools.tagline: Set up schools and their branches

createSchool.title: Create a school
createSchool.summary: A school is the identity: its name and leadership. The actual daily work happens in its branches.
createSchool.step1: Go to Schools and press the add button.
createSchool.step2: Enter the school name and the principal's name and phone; optionally add the official phone and address (printed on document mastheads — branch values win when set) and the school logo.
createSchool.step3: Optionally add a technical contact for setup questions.
createSchool.step4: Save — the school appears in the list. Next, add its first branch.

addBranch.title: Add a branch
addBranch.summary: The branch is where students, employees, fees and attendance actually live. Every school needs at least one.
addBranch.step1: Open Branches and press the add button (or add from the school's page).
addBranch.step2: Fill in the basics — name and code — and the location: city, sub-city, woreda.
addBranch.step3: Enter the director's name and phone; they get access once their employee record with a director position exists.
addBranch.step4: In “Grades & programs offered”, tick which grades the branch teaches under each education program (e.g. Grade 1 → Regular + Night). By default every grade is on under Regular; add program columns with the chips and use the column or cycle checkboxes to bulk-tick.
addBranch.step5: Save, then switch into the new branch with the school/branch switcher to set it up.
addBranch.tip: Branches are strictly separated: a teacher or student in one branch is invisible from another. The grades you tick here also drive every grade filter the branch's staff see — a KG-only branch never shows Grade 12 anywhere. Grades with live enrollments or sections lock and can't be unticked until those are moved.

profileStats.title: Read the school & branch profiles
profileStats.summary: Every school and branch has a profile with live vitals: students, teachers, workforce by job title, guardians, sections and the subjects taught.
profileStats.step1: The Schools and Branches tables already show the essentials per row — branches, grades served (e.g. KG-1 – Grade 12), students and teachers. Sort by any count.
profileStats.step2: Click a row to open the profile. The school profile is split into tabs: Overview (vitals and charts), Branches (the branch list) and Settings. The tiles on top show attending students (with pending registrations), teachers, all employees, reachable guardians, sections with seats, and subjects taught — tap any tile to jump straight to that module (students, employees, guardians, sections). Under Settings, the school defaults are grouped into their own tabs — Academic policy, Attendance & alerts, Fees & discounts and Finance controls — so it is no longer one long form.
profileStats.step3: Below, charts break the picture down: a boys/girls donut with the attending total, active employees ranked by job title, and a students-per-grade chart (hover a grade to see its sections too).
profileStats.step4: On a school profile, the branch list carries the same numbers per branch — click a branch row to drill into its own profile.
profileStats.tip: The vitals refresh every few minutes. Only students on a roster count as attending; pending registrations are shown separately.
profileStats.step5: The school logo on the profile hero is managed by Temari.et platform staff only — it prints on official documents (transcripts, report cards), so schools request changes rather than editing it themselves.

branchStatus.title: Activate or deactivate a branch
branchStatus.summary: Deactivating pauses a branch without losing anything.
branchStatus.step1: Find the branch in the list and open its row actions.
branchStatus.step2: Deactivate to freeze it — the branch is kept but hidden from daily work.
branchStatus.step3: Reactivate any time; nothing is deleted in between.

rolesExplained.title: How roles & access work
rolesExplained.summary: Access in Temari is always a role plus a place. Nobody has power somewhere they weren't given it.
rolesExplained.step1: A role only works where it was granted: a principal at School A has zero access at School B.
rolesExplained.step2: School roles (Principal, School admin) cover every branch of their school.
rolesExplained.step3: Branch roles (Director, Registrar, Finance officer, Teacher) apply to exactly one branch.
rolesExplained.step4: Parents and students are not employees — they see their own children's or their own data through being linked to a student.
rolesExplained.tip: Employee access follows HR: adding a teacher / director / registrar / finance officer position grants the matching access automatically — see Employees & HR.

addUser.title: Add a user
addUser.summary: Create an account and place it: which role, at which school or branch.
addUser.step1: Go to Users and press the add button.
addUser.step2: Enter the full name — first, father's and grandfather's name — and the phone number they will sign in with.
addUser.step3: Assign a role and pick exactly where it applies: the school, or a single branch.
addUser.step4: Save. The person signs in with their phone number and sets their own PIN.

accountActions.title: Manage an account
accountActions.summary: Everything you need when someone is locked out, leaves, or misbehaves.
accountActions.step1: Open the row actions on any user to edit, reset their PIN, or deactivate them.
accountActions.step2: Reset PIN when someone is locked out — they set a new one at their next sign-in.
accountActions.step3: Deactivate blocks sign-in but keeps all history; you can reactivate any time.
accountActions.step4: Ban is for abuse only — it blocks the account everywhere on the platform.

bulkActions.title: Do the same thing to many people at once
bulkActions.summary: Tick the people you need, then act on the whole selection from the bar at the bottom of the screen.
bulkActions.step1: Tick the box on each row you want — on a phone, tap Select first, then tap the rows.
bulkActions.step2: A bar appears at the bottom showing how many are selected and what you can do with them.
bulkActions.step3: School leaders get Branch access: put everyone selected into a branch with the job roles you tick, or turn their access to that branch off and back on.
bulkActions.step4: Temari staff also get Activate, Deactivate, Ban, Reset password, Delete and Restore for the whole selection.
bulkActions.step5: Confirm when asked. You are told how many succeeded — and if anyone was skipped, who they were and why.
bulkActions.step6: Deleted someone by mistake? Turn on the Deleted filter → "Show deleted accounts", tick the rows, and press Restore. They come back with exactly the access they had.
bulkActions.tip: Nobody outside your authority is ever changed, and your own account is always left alone — so a wide selection is safe. Filter or search first, then tick the top box to select everything on the page.

studentParentAccounts.title: Student & parent accounts in the directory
studentParentAccounts.summary: Students and parents with logins appear in Users alongside employees, with chips showing why the account exists.
studentParentAccounts.step1: A "Student" chip shows where they study (school · branch · grade); a "Parent" chip shows their children.
studentParentAccounts.step2: School employees see these accounts only while the student is actively enrolled at their school — when the student leaves, the row disappears on its own.
studentParentAccounts.step3: These rows are read-only for school employees: editing identity, banning or deleting an account is Temari platform-only, because the same person may also be a parent at another school.
studentParentAccounts.step4: To check whether one student or parent can log in, open the student's profile — the "Portal account" chip on the student page and on each guardian card shows Active, Never logged in, or No login.
studentParentAccounts.tip: Filter the Users table by the Student or Parent role to audit which families have working logins.

createYear.title: Create an academic year
createYear.summary: The year is the calendar backbone: it owns the semesters everything else anchors to.
createYear.step1: Go to Academic years and press the add button.
createYear.step2: The name is suggested from the Ethiopian calendar; set the start and end dates.
createYear.step3: Choose how many semesters the year runs — they are created for you.
createYear.step4: The year starts as Planned: set everything up freely, nothing shows in daily work yet.
createYear.step5: When ready, set it to Active — it becomes the current year for the branch.

lifecycle.title: The year & semester lifecycle
lifecycle.summary: Years and semesters move through Planned → Active → Closed. This protects your records.
lifecycle.step1: Planned is for setup, Active is the one daily work happens in, Closed is read-only history.
lifecycle.step2: Activating a semester closes the previous one — exactly one is active at a time.
lifecycle.step3: Closed semesters are locked everywhere: attendance, assignments and grades in them can't be changed.
lifecycle.step4: Nothing is lost — closed periods stay fully viewable for reports and history.
lifecycle.tip: If saving fails with a "semester is closed" message, you're editing a past period — switch to the current semester.

assignments.title: Assign teachers (semester grid)
assignments.summary: Each semester has a grid of every section × subject in the branch. Fill it so every class has a teacher.
assignments.step1: Open Semesters and click into the semester.
assignments.step2: Pick a grade tab at the top, then a section tab under it — the card below shows that section's subjects. Use Next section to walk through them like app screens.
assignments.step3: Pick a teacher per cell — amber "unassigned" chips show what's still missing.
assignments.step4: Assign one teacher to many cells at once instead of clicking one by one.
assignments.step5: These assignments drive what teachers see: their own sections, attendance lists and continuous assessments.

cloneCopy.title: Reuse last semester's setup
cloneCopy.summary: Don't rebuild the teacher grid every semester — clone or copy it.
cloneCopy.step1: Open the actions on a semester to see Clone and Copy.
cloneCopy.step2: Clone semester creates a new semester with the same settings and the full assignment grid.
cloneCopy.step3: Copy semester from… pulls another semester's teacher grid into the one you're on.
cloneCopy.step4: Review the grid afterwards — employees who left leave gaps to fill.
cloneCopy.tip: Copying never changes the source semester; it only fills the current one.

createSection.title: Create sections
createSection.summary: Sections are the classes students sit in — Grade 5 A, Grade 5 B, and so on.
createSection.step1: Go to Sections and press the add button.
createSection.step2: Pick the grade level and give the section a name (A, B, …) and a capacity.
createSection.step3: The grades offered come from the programs chosen on the branch.
createSection.step4: Create sections before enrolling students — enrollment asks for a section.

homeroom.title: Set a homeroom teacher
homeroom.summary: Each section can have a homeroom teacher per academic year.
homeroom.step1: Open a section and pick the homeroom teacher for the academic year.
homeroom.step2: Only employees with an active teaching position can be chosen.
homeroom.step3: Homerooms are per year — when a new year starts, set them again.
homeroom.tip: Past years keep their homeroom history; changing this year never rewrites last year.

assignSections.title: Distribute students into sections
assignSections.summary: The section-assignment board deals a grade's students into balanced classes — even gender split, even ability spread — then you fine-tune and save.
assignSections.step1: Open Sections → Assign sections, pick the year and grade.
assignSections.step2: Press Auto-balance: Fill empty seats places only unassigned students; Reshuffle everyone redeals the whole grade.
assignSections.step3: Each column shows count, capacity, boys/girls and average — move any student with a tap.
assignSections.step4: Unsaved moves are highlighted; nothing is stored yet.
assignSections.step5: Press Save assignments to commit everything at once.
assignSections.tip: After the year rollover, continuing students keep their section letter automatically — the board is mainly for new students and rebalancing.

bulkAssign.title: Assign students from the register
bulkAssign.summary: Hand-pick any set of students on the Students page and move them into a section in one go — or pull them back to the unassigned pool to decide later.
bulkAssign.step1: On Students, tick the students (filters help — e.g. filter a grade first).
bulkAssign.step2: Press Assign to section in the floating bar.
bulkAssign.step3: Pick the year, grade and target section — or switch to Remove from section to return them to the pool.
bulkAssign.step4: Students enrolled in another grade or year are skipped automatically and reported — the rest move.
bulkAssign.tip: Leaving students unassigned is fine: they keep their enrollment and appear in the section-assignment board's pool until you place them.

classProfile.title: Open the class profile
classProfile.summary: Clicking a section opens its class profile: every student on the roster with gender, age, semester average out of 100, rank and conduct.
classProfile.step1: Go to Sections and click any row — the class profile opens.
classProfile.step2: Pick the semester at the top right; the roster and marks follow it.
classProfile.step3: The cards show the class size (boys/girls), class average, pass rate and subject count; the homeroom teacher is one tap away for a call.
classProfile.step4: Click a student to open their profile; use Export for a printable class list.
classProfile.tip: Averages come from the frozen semester results — press Compute on Report cards first if the semester is still open.

teacherView.title: What teachers can see
teacherView.summary: Teachers see only their own classes — the school-wide registers stay with office roles.
teacherView.step1: The Sections page lists only the classes you teach or hold as homeroom this year.
teacherView.step2: Attendance registers and class profiles open for those sections only.
teacherView.step3: Student and parent registers, fees and school-wide reports belong to office roles (registrar, director, principal).
teacherView.tip: Missing one of your classes? Ask your director to check your subject assignments or homeroom for the active year.

register.title: Register a student (guided)
register.summary: Four fast steps: student, guardians, enrollment & fees, review — health and documents are optional extras you can add now or later.
register.step1: Go to Students and press Register student — a four-step wizard opens.
register.step2: Step 1 (Student): names, gender, date of birth, address; optionally photo, languages, IDs, phone. Health info and documents sit under "More details (optional)" — open it only if the family brought them.
register.step3: Step 2 (Guardians): search Temari.et first by ID code or phone so an existing parent is reused, not duplicated.
register.step4: Step 3 (Enrollment & fees): pick the academic year and grade (the section can wait), the previous school, and the fees that apply — mark each as unpaid, collected now, or a scholarship.
register.step5: Step 4: review and submit. Guardians get an SMS: a sign-up link for new accounts, a notice for existing ones.
register.step6: Anything skipped shows as an "Add health info" / "Add documents" chip on the student profile — tap it any time to finish the file.
register.tip: Every student and every account gets a public ID code like H8R6WV — tap it anywhere in the app to copy it; it works at any Temari.et school.

bulkImport.title: Import students from Excel (bulk)
bulkImport.summary: Bring a whole register in at once: upload a spreadsheet, match its columns, fix what the checker flags, then import — with SMS off by default so no family is texted by mistake.
bulkImport.step1: Go to Students and press Import. Pick the academic year (and optionally a default grade and section if the whole file is one class), then drop in your .xlsx, .xls or .csv file. The file is read on your device — nothing is uploaded yet. You can also download our ready-made template.
bulkImport.step2: Match the file's columns to Temari fields. Columns we recognize match themselves — including Amharic headers. A single "Full name" column is split into first, father and grandfather names automatically.
bulkImport.step3: If birth dates are in the Ethiopian calendar, pick the Ethiopian date format — a live preview shows how each date converts. Grade values like "1", "Grade 1" or "ክፍል 1" are recognized; anything unclear is listed once for you to assign.
bulkImport.step4: Press Check rows. Every row is checked on the server: missing or invalid values are flagged red, students who already exist at your school show as duplicates, and a guardian phone that already has a Temari account is noted — that parent will be linked, never duplicated.
bulkImport.step5: Fix flagged rows right in the grid — click a row, correct the fields, save. For each duplicate decide: skip it (default), enroll the existing student into this year, or create anyway for a genuine namesake.
bulkImport.step6: Press Import. Choose whether to create student login accounts, and whether to send SMS to families — this is OFF by default, and the confirmation states it plainly. The import runs in the background; you get a notification with the report, and any failed rows can be downloaded, fixed and re-uploaded alone.
bulkImport.tip: Import runs never text families unless you switch SMS on — a wrong file cannot become an SMS storm. Registration fees still apply: imported enrollments follow your school's registration-fee gate exactly like wizard registrations.

enroll.title: Enroll a student
enroll.summary: Enrollment ties a student to an academic year and a grade; the section can be assigned later.
enroll.step1: From the student's page or list, open Enroll.
enroll.step2: Pick the academic year and grade level; add the section now or later.
enroll.step3: Record the previous school from the directory when the student transferred in.
enroll.step4: Each new year needs a new enrollment; every past year stays on the record.
enroll.step5: Picked the wrong grade by mistake? On the student's page, press the pencil next to the enrollment to change its grade or section in place. Once semester results are frozen the grade locks — it becomes history.

guardians.title: Link parents & guardians
guardians.summary: Guardians are how parents follow their child — and how the school reaches families. At least one guardian is required — the last one can't be removed.
guardians.step1: On the student's Guardians tab, press Add guardian.
guardians.step2: Search Temari.et first — by ID code (e.g. H8R6WV), phone or name. A parent registered at any school is reused.
guardians.step3: If they're new, enter their names and phone; they get an SMS link to create their account.
guardians.step4: Choose per guardian what they may do: view grades, view attendance, pay fees, receive SMS.
guardians.tip: A parent with children at different Temari.et schools sees them all under one account — never create a second account for the same person.
guardians.step5: To fix a guardian's details later (name, phone, email, occupation), press the pencil on their card in the Guardians tab.

healthDocs.title: Health records & documents
healthDocs.summary: Health conditions and files live on the student's page, visible only to employees who may view students.
healthDocs.step1: Open the student's Health tab to see conditions, severity and medication.
healthDocs.step2: Press Edit on the Health tab to add or change conditions — pick from the standard list, set severity and medication, and add notes.
healthDocs.step3: Use the Documents tab to attach files and label each with its type — birth certificate, vaccination card (ketebat), kebele ID, National ID (Fayda), transfer certificate… (PDF or photo, up to 10 MB).
healthDocs.step4: Files are stored privately; tap any file to preview it right on the page — images zoom, PDFs open inline — and use the toolbar to download or share it.

parentsRegister.title: The parents register
parentsRegister.summary: Every guardian linked to your students, in one place — with photos, files and their children.
parentsRegister.step1: Open Parents (next to Students). Search by name, ID code, phone or email.
parentsRegister.step2: Click a parent to open their profile: children, contact details, documents.
parentsRegister.step3: Add a photo or ID documents from the profile — files are stored privately.

pendingActivation.title: Pending enrollments & the registration fee
pendingActivation.summary: A new enrollment stays pending until the registration fee is paid or covered by a scholarship — the student holds a seat but appears on no class list. School policy decides how strict this is.
pendingActivation.step1: Register or promote a student — if a registration fee applies, the enrollment starts pending and the invoice is issued automatically.
pendingActivation.step2: Recording the payment (or a full scholarship) activates the enrollment instantly.
pendingActivation.step3: Under the soft policy, employees can activate early from the student's row (Activate enrollment) — the invoice stays open with its reminders.
pendingActivation.step4: Under the hard policy only payment or a scholarship activates.
pendingActivation.tip: Set the policy in School profile → Academic policy. Soft is the default and matches how most schools actually operate.

portalLogins.title: Portal logins for families
portalLogins.summary: Who can sign in, how to create a student login (own phone or student ID), and how self-signup claims work.
portalLogins.step1: Every profile shows a Portal account chip: No login, Invite sent (account created, PIN link texted), Never logged in, or Active with the last sign-in date.
portalLogins.step2: Guardians get their account automatically at registration — created with the guardian's OWN phone. If the chip says No login, press "Send setup link" to re-text the PIN link.
portalLogins.step3: Students with their own phone get an SMS-keyed login: press "Add login account", pick "Own phone" and enter the student's OWN number — a guardian's number is always rejected.
portalLogins.step4: Students WITHOUT a phone get an ID login: pick "Student ID" instead. They sign in with their 6-character Temari ID + PIN; the setup SMS (with the ID and PIN link) goes to the primary guardian.
portalLogins.step5: If someone signs up on temari.et with a Temari ID but an unknown phone, a "Login claims" button appears on the Students page. Approve only after confirming who they are.
portalLogins.tip: Every new registration now creates a login automatically — an SMS-keyed one when the student has their own phone, otherwise a student ID + PIN login. “Add login account” is for students registered before this or imported without accounts.

createEmployee.title: Add an employee
createEmployee.summary: The employee record is the person's HR file at your branch: identity, employment and qualifications.
createEmployee.step1: Go to Employees and press the add button.
createEmployee.step2: Identity: photo (optional), full name and phone number.
createEmployee.step3: Employment: hire date, employment type and base salary.
createEmployee.step4: Qualifications: education level, field of study, institution.
createEmployee.step5: Save — the HR file is created for this branch.

positions.title: Positions & what they unlock
positions.summary: Positions are the jobs a person holds. They are also how branch employees get app access.
positions.step1: An employee holds one or more positions — holding several at once is normal.
positions.step2: Add a position with its title and start date; end it when the job ends.
positions.step3: Teacher, Director, Registrar and Finance officer positions grant the matching app access at the branch automatically.
positions.step4: Ending such a position removes that access just as automatically.
positions.tip: Don't hand out branch roles from the Users page — access follows the HR position, so HR stays the single source of truth.

compensation.title: Salary, allowances & documents
compensation.summary: Everything payroll needs lives on the employee's file.
compensation.step1: The base salary sits in the employment details.
compensation.step2: Add allowances — taxable or not — and they flow into payroll automatically.
compensation.step3: Attach documents such as contracts and certificates to the file.
compensation.step4: Changes apply to the next payroll run; already-approved runs never change.

teachingLoad.title: See what a teacher teaches
teachingLoad.summary: Every teacher's profile shows their real workload for a semester: subjects, sections, weekly periods and their published timetable.
teachingLoad.step1: Go to Employees and open the teacher's profile.
teachingLoad.step2: The Teaching load card lists each subject with its sections, weekly periods and student counts — plus their homeroom, if they hold one.
teachingLoad.step3: Use the semester picker on the card to look at a past or upcoming semester.
teachingLoad.step4: Once the semester's timetable is published, the teacher's personal weekly schedule appears below (on a phone, pick a day to see that day's lessons).
teachingLoad.tip: This card reads from the semester's teaching grid. To change who teaches what, open the semester and edit the grid there.

hr.title: HR & leave
hr.tagline: Employee attendance, leave and the school’s HR policy

employeeAttendance.title: Take employee attendance
employeeAttendance.summary: One daily register for all branch employees, with approved leave filled in automatically.
employeeAttendance.step1: Open Employee attendance and pick the date (today by default).
employeeAttendance.step2: Every active employee of the branch is listed. Employees on approved leave show a blue on-leave chip — no mark needed.
employeeAttendance.step3: Use Mark all present, then change only the exceptions: Late, Half day, Absent or Excused.
employeeAttendance.step4: Optionally record check-in / check-out times and a short note per person.
employeeAttendance.step5: Save. Reopen the same day any time to correct it.
employeeAttendance.tip: Holidays and weekends are flagged on the register, and they never count against anyone's leave.

requestLeave.title: Request leave (HR)
requestLeave.summary: Every employee requests their own leave and follows its status from HR.
requestLeave.step1: Open HR — your balances per leave type are on top (e.g. 12 of 16 annual days left).
requestLeave.step2: Tap Request leave, pick the type and the first / last day.
requestLeave.step3: Weekends and school holidays are not counted — the form previews the working days used.
requestLeave.step4: Some types (like sick leave) require a note, e.g. a medical certificate number.
requestLeave.step5: Submit. You can cancel it any time while it is still pending.
requestLeave.tip: Annual leave follows the labour law: 16 working days, growing by 1 day for every 2 years of service.

approveLeave.title: Approve or reject leave
approveLeave.summary: Directors and school admins decide requests; balances are enforced automatically.
approveLeave.step1: Open Leave. Pending requests are listed first — filter by status or type.
approveLeave.step2: Open a request's actions and choose Approve or Reject.
approveLeave.step3: Rejecting requires a note so the employee always knows why.
approveLeave.step4: Approvals that exceed the remaining balance are blocked — an explicit override checkbox is offered.
approveLeave.step5: Approved leave appears on the employee register automatically for those dates.
approveLeave.tip: You can also submit a request on behalf of any employee from the Leave page.

policyHolidays.title: Leave policy & holidays
policyHolidays.summary: The leave-type catalog and the holiday calendar are school-wide settings.
policyHolidays.step1: Open Leave → Policy & holidays. The first visit seeds the Ethiopian labour-law defaults (annual, sick, maternity…).
policyHolidays.step2: Adjust days per year, paid/unpaid, who it applies to, or add your own types.
policyHolidays.step3: A type that has been used is deactivated instead of deleted, so history keeps its meaning.
policyHolidays.step4: Add holidays (Meskel, Eid, closures…) — they are skipped by leave day counts and flagged on the register.
policyHolidays.tip: Holidays can apply to the whole school or one branch only.

teacherAppraisals.title: Teacher performance appraisals
teacherAppraisals.summary: The per-semester appraisal in the Ministry of Education format — scored on the school’s rubric, shared with the teacher, and signed digitally.
teacherAppraisals.step1: Directors and principals open HR → Teacher appraisals, pick the semester and press New appraisal.
teacherAppraisals.step2: The sheet lists the school’s criteria (lesson planning, teaching methods, assessment, ethics…). Tap a rating for each line and add evidence notes; the overall score out of 100 updates live.
teacherAppraisals.step3: The sheet also shows platform facts — how many marklists and weekly lesson plans the teacher had approved this semester — as context, never as an automatic score.
teacherAppraisals.step4: Write strengths and areas to improve, then press Share with teacher. The teacher is notified; a shared appraisal can no longer be edited.
teacherAppraisals.step5: The teacher opens My appraisals, reviews every score, optionally writes a response, and presses Acknowledge — the digital signature.
teacherAppraisals.step6: To change the criteria or weights, use the gear icon on the register. Weights must total 100; past appraisals keep the criteria they were scored on.
teacherAppraisals.tip: One appraisal per employee per semester. The register’s history across semesters is the growth record for career-ladder paperwork.

hrReports.title: Read the HR reports
hrReports.summary: Headcount, attendance rate, leave usage and payroll cost in one place.
hrReports.step1: Open HR reports and pick the window — use the This month / Last month / Last 30 days presets or a custom range.
hrReports.step2: The cards summarise active employees, attendance rate, approved leave days and the latest payroll cost.
hrReports.step3: Below: charts for the daily register, weekday absence patterns, leave by month, payroll cost history and employee tenure — then composition and a per-person attendance table.
hrReports.step4: Search the table by name, filter by job title or attendance rate, and export it for records or payroll evidence.

runPayroll.title: Run payroll
runPayroll.summary: A payroll run gathers every active employee's pay for a period and computes tax and pension for you.
runPayroll.step1: Go to Payroll, press the add button, and give the run a name and period.
runPayroll.step2: Every active employee is added with gross pay, income tax, pension and net pay.
runPayroll.step3: Open the run and review each person's breakdown.
runPayroll.step4: Changed a salary or allowance? Recompute refreshes a draft run.
runPayroll.step5: Income tax follows the current Ethiopian tax tables; pension is 7% employee and 11% employer.

approvePay.title: Approve & pay
approvePay.summary: Approval freezes the run permanently — that snapshot is your payroll record.
approvePay.step1: Approve the run once every item is reviewed — the numbers are frozen exactly as shown.
approvePay.step2: Salary or allowance edits after approval never change an approved run.
approvePay.step3: Mark the run as paid once the money has gone out.
approvePay.step4: Corrections to an approved run are made in a following run, never by editing history.
approvePay.tip: Approval is deliberately final — it's what makes your payroll records trustworthy.

record.title: Take attendance
record.summary: One register per section per day, four statuses, done in under a minute.
record.step1: Open Attendance, pick the section and the date.
record.step2: Every student enrolled in the section is listed.
record.step3: Use Mark all present, then change only the exceptions.
record.step4: Statuses: Present, Absent, Late and Excused.
record.step5: Optionally record check-in / check-out times and a short note per student.
record.step6: Save. Reopen the same day any time to correct it.
record.tip: Attendance can only be recorded in the active semester — closed semesters are read-only. Teachers can open only the register of the section they homeroom.

reports.title: Attendance reports
reports.summary: Trends, absences and capture methods across your scope — a branch, the whole school, or your own sections.
reports.step1: Open Attendance reports. Directors see their branch, principals the whole school (narrowable to one branch), Temari.et staff the whole platform, and teachers their homeroom sections.
reports.step2: Pick the window — the last 7, 15 or 30 days, this month, a whole semester, quarter or academic year from the term picker, or any custom range. Every number compares against the previous window of the same length.
reports.step3: Filter by grade, section, capture method (RFID device or manual register) or one specific terminal.
reports.step4: Work through the three tabs: Overview (headline cards, daily register, comparison table), Patterns (weekday, capture method and arrival-time charts) and Students (the per-student ledger).
reports.step5: The student table lists everyone in scope — sort by absences, search a name, use the Chronic absentees or Perfect attendance pills, and export to CSV or Excel.
reports.tip: A student is flagged chronically absent after missing 10% or more of their recorded days. Tap the Chronic absentees card to jump straight to that list, and tap a row to open the student's profile.

excuses.title: Review absence excuses
excuses.summary: Parents file excuses for absences; approving marks those days excused.
excuses.step1: Open Absence excuses under Operations — pending requests sort first.
excuses.step2: Read the reason and open the attached proof if the family provided one.
excuses.step3: Approve or Reject, optionally adding a note the family will see.
excuses.step4: Approving flips the range's Absent days to Excused automatically; the family is notified either way.
excuses.tip: Only recorded absences change — presence and lateness stay exactly as marked.

devices.title: Devices & ID cards
devices.tagline: RFID gates, MIFARE cards and parent alerts

setupDevice.title: Set up an attendance terminal
setupDevice.summary: Register the device, give it its token, and watch scans arrive — it works offline and syncs when data returns.
setupDevice.step1: Open Devices & cards → Devices and press Register device.
setupDevice.step2: Name it (e.g. Main gate), pick its branch, and choose who it serves: students, employees or both.
setupDevice.step3: Copy the access token into the terminal — it is shown only once.
setupDevice.step4: The status dot turns green when the device phones home; Scans today counts its taps.
setupDevice.step5: Use the Scan log tab to see every tap and why any scan was rejected.
setupDevice.tip: Offline is normal: the terminal queues scans and uploads them when mobile data returns — duplicates are ignored automatically.

issueCards.title: Cards: Temari.et issues, schools report
issueCards.summary: Physical cards are printed and delivered by Temari.et. Schools report lost cards and follow the replacement request.
issueCards.step1: Cards and terminals are supplied by Temari.et — schools view their register under Devices & cards but cannot issue cards themselves.
issueCards.step2: Temari.et staff use Bulk issue to card a whole branch: pick the branch, then tap chips down the worklist in scan mode.
issueCards.step3: If a card is lost or damaged, press Report lost — scans reject it instantly and a replacement request is sent to Temari.et with your note.
issueCards.step4: Follow the request in the Card requests tab: Requested → Accepted → Preparing card → Delivering → Delivered.
issueCards.step5: Until the replacement arrives, mark that person on the normal register — manual entries always win over scans.
issueCards.tip: One person holds exactly one active card. The lost chip stays blocked forever, so a found card cannot be misused.

guardianAlerts.title: Parent absence alerts
guardianAlerts.summary: Guardians are texted (and emailed) the moment their child is marked absent — automatically, in their own language.
guardianAlerts.step1: Alerts are on by default. School managers set the default under the school profile; Branch settings can override per branch.
guardianAlerts.step2: Choose whether late arrivals also alert — absent-only is the default.
guardianAlerts.step3: With gate devices, enable Auto-absent: students with no scan by the cutoff are marked absent and parents are alerted.
guardianAlerts.step4: The Alerts sent tab shows every message with a monthly SMS counter.
guardianAlerts.step5: A guardian is texted at most once per child per day per reason — re-saving a register never double-texts.
guardianAlerts.tip: Alerts respect each guardian's link settings and their own notification preferences — and only ever fire for today, never for backfilled days.

gradingSetup.title: Choose how marks are graded
gradingSetup.summary: Grading scales map raw marks to letters and pass/fail; rules decide which scale each grade range uses.
gradingSetup.step1: Open Grading under Academic. Platform scales (Percentage, Ethiopian Letter A–F, Early Grades) are ready to use.
gradingSetup.step2: Add a school scale only if your school grades differently — define each band's range, letter, label and pass mark.
gradingSetup.step3: Under "Where scales apply", add a rule: pick the scale, what report cards show (numbers, letters or both) and the grade range.
gradingSetup.step4: School-wide rules apply everywhere; a branch rule overrides them for that branch only.
gradingSetup.step5: Grades without a rule use the numeric percentage scale automatically.
gradingSetup.tip: Marks are always stored as numbers — letters are how they are displayed, so you can switch a scale without losing anything.

continuousAssessment.title: Create a continuous assessment plan
continuousAssessment.summary: The principal or director defines the plan; every teacher's marklist follows it automatically.
continuousAssessment.step1: Open Continuous assessment and press Create plan.
continuousAssessment.step2: Pick the semester, then under “Applies to” add a grade row for each grade the plan covers. For each grade choose its sections (or leave “All sections”) and its subjects (or leave “All subjects”). Leave a single “All grades” row to cover the whole branch, or press “Add grade” for a different combination. The same grade + section + subject can belong to only one plan in a semester — layer a more specific plan (e.g. for one subject) instead of repeating a combination.
continuousAssessment.step3: Add the assessment slots — e.g. Quiz 10%, Assignment 15%, Mid exam 25%, Final exam 50%. Drag the handle at the left of a row to reorder them.
continuousAssessment.step4: Weights must add up to exactly 100 before you can save.
continuousAssessment.step5: Teachers now find these assessments waiting in their marklists and cannot change the structure.
continuousAssessment.tip: Without a plan, teachers may define their own assessments only when the branch setting “Teacher-defined assessments” is on (weights still capped at 100).
continuousAssessment.step6: If the new plan overlaps an existing one, the app warns you and asks how to continue: replace (start fresh — overlapping marks are deleted) or keep matching marks (they move onto same-type assessments).

enterMarks.title: Enter marks (teachers)
enterMarks.summary: One grid per subject and section: type scores, mark absentees, save, submit.
enterMarks.step1: Open Marklists — every subject you teach this semester is listed.
enterMarks.step2: Open a marklist. Students are the rows, assessments the columns.
enterMarks.step3: Type each score (never above the assessment's maximum). Use the A button for absent students.
enterMarks.step4: Save marks as you go — unsaved cells are highlighted.
enterMarks.step5: Beside each mark the grid shows the weighted score it converts to (mark ÷ maximum × weight) — the Weighted button shows or hides it. The Total column adds these weighted scores out of the term's full weight; that is the number report cards use. On the phone each student's total appears under their name as a progress bar with the score — it updates as you type and shows the change in green or red.
enterMarks.step6: When the marklist is complete, press Submit for approval.
enterMarks.step7: Your draft is yours alone — a director cannot quietly change it. If a director entered marks on your behalf, an amber banner names them with their reason, each of their marks carries an amber dot, and the submit window lists them — review before you submit, because submitting confirms every mark.
enterMarks.tip: After submitting, marks lock. Ask your director to reopen the marklist if you need a correction.

approveMarklists.title: Approve marklists (directors)
approveMarklists.summary: The digital countersign: review submitted marklists, approve or send back.
approveMarklists.step1: Open Marklists — you see every subject and section with its status.
approveMarklists.step2: Filter by Submitted to get the approval queue. An amber pen icon means marks were entered on the teacher's behalf.
approveMarklists.step3: Open a marklist to review the marks, then press Approve.
approveMarklists.step4: Use Reopen to send it back to draft when a correction is needed — approving locks it.
approveMarklists.step5: If you entered any marks on that sheet yourself, the app hides Approve and asks a different supervisor to countersign — nobody approves their own entries.
approveMarklists.tip: Only print report cards once every marklist of the section is approved.

enterOnBehalf.title: Enter marks on a teacher's behalf
enterOnBehalf.summary: A teacher's draft is read-only for supervisors — on-behalf entry is the loud, recorded exception.
enterOnBehalf.step1: Open the teacher's marklist. While it is their draft you can read everything but type nothing.
enterOnBehalf.step2: Press "Enter on behalf" and write the reason (for example, the teacher is on sick leave). The teacher is notified immediately, with your reason.
enterOnBehalf.step3: Type the marks — every one you enter is labeled with your name, dotted in the grid, and shown to the teacher and the approver.
enterOnBehalf.step4: A different supervisor must approve that marklist — you cannot countersign your own entries.
enterOnBehalf.tip: Classes with no teacher account (a vacancy) skip the declaration — supervisors enter marks directly.

reportCards.title: Conduct, comments & extra assessment
reportCards.summary: Conduct (ሥነ ምግባር), the homeroom comment and the behavioral skill checklist are entered right on the roster — and print on the report cards.
reportCards.step1: On the Rosters page, type conduct (A–E) straight into the Conduct column and press Save conduct — the quick lane for a whole class.
reportCards.step2: Open a row's Extra assessment to enter the homeroom comment and rate the school's skill checklist (E / VG / S / NI) per term.
reportCards.step3: On the yearly tab the same surface shows one pill per term or quarter — each column of the printed yearly card is edited there.
reportCards.step4: The checklist itself is school policy: School settings → Report cards lets a manager add suggested Ethiopian rows or custom ones, in all three languages (branches may override).
reportCards.step5: The same settings section controls cards-per-page (1 relaxed, 2 stacked halves or 4 wallet cards per sheet), per-subject ranks on the semester card and the grading-criteria legend on the yearly card.
reportCards.step6: Absence days come from the attendance register automatically; closed semesters are read-only.
reportCards.tip: Skill ratings and conduct survive recomputes — the freeze never touches what the homeroom teacher entered.

rosters.title: Rosters — results, report cards & printing
rosters.summary: One hub for the semester and yearly roster: every mark, total, average and rank, with report-card printing, transcripts and bulk actions on each row.
rosters.step1: Open Rosters under Academic and choose Semester or Yearly at the top (school managers pick the branch first).
rosters.step2: Pick the semester (or academic year), then a grade — optionally narrow to one section. Search, sort and page like any register.
rosters.step3: Each row shows the marks per subject, total, average, rank, conduct and absent days; failing marks are tinted red.
rosters.step4: Use the row's Report card action to Download or Print the official PDF — on the yearly tab, choose Both (the full duplex booklet), or just the Inside (marks & assessment) or Cover (front & remarks) side.
rosters.step5: Tick several students (or Select all) to print their report cards or transcripts as ONE PDF — up to 60 students per batch.
rosters.step6: The Transcript action opens the student's multi-year transcript; Export still gives the CSV or the roster-sheet PDF of the whole list.
rosters.step7: Recompute (grades.manage) refreshes a preview while the semester is open — results freeze automatically when it closes.
rosters.tip: Everything prints from the FROZEN results, so the roster, the report cards and the QR-verified copies always agree.

transcripts.title: Transcripts (view, bulk print & export)
transcripts.summary: The transcript register: pick a class, check readiness, view one transcript or print/export a whole selection — every print is an official PDF.
transcripts.step1: Open Academic → Transcripts and pick the academic year and grade (school managers pick the branch first); optionally narrow to one section.
transcripts.step2: The readiness column shows how many years and semesters of frozen results each student has — 'No results yet' means nothing is computed.
transcripts.step3: Use the Transcript button on a row to open that student's printable transcript in a new tab (also available on the Students list and profile).
transcripts.step4: Use the Years covered picker to narrow which academic years print — the default is the complete record; a subset is stamped 'Partial transcript' on the sheet and on its QR verify page. The same picker appears on each student's transcript page next to Download PDF.
transcripts.step5: Printing and Download PDF both use the OFFICIAL backend-rendered PDF — pixel-perfect on paper. Its QR opens the live transcript online (same page, no login), so anyone holding the paper can verify it; revoking the document kills that link.
transcripts.tip: Transcripts read the same frozen results as report cards — recompute a semester on the Report Cards page if today's marks are missing.
transcripts.step6: Select several rows and choose Print transcripts. A preview opens with one sheet per student; Download PDF / Print there give you the whole class as ONE official PDF, one student per page (up to 60 students per run — print a section at a time).
transcripts.step7: Export Excel turns the selection into a flat sheet: one row per student per year with semester and annual averages.

gradingAnalytics.title: Grading reports & exports
gradingAnalytics.summary: Term analytics from the frozen results: trends, highlights, distribution, subjects, sections and follow-up lists.
gradingAnalytics.step1: Open Grading Reports and pick the semester (school managers pick the branch first).
gradingAnalytics.step2: The cards show students, average and pass rate — including the change since the previous semester — plus approved marklists.
gradingAnalytics.step3: Highlights surface the best section, toughest subject, boys/girls pass rates and average absence days; charts break performance down by band, subject and section.
gradingAnalytics.step4: Narrow with the grade and section pickers — every number on the page follows the selection.
gradingAnalytics.step5: Top students and Needs attention list who leads and who is below the pass line; Export CSV downloads all the aggregates.
gradingAnalytics.tip: Numbers here always match issued report cards — both read the same frozen results.

marklistAnalysis.title: Marklist analysis
marklistAnalysis.summary: Per-subject performance for a cohort: adjustable score ranges with a boys/girls split, top performers and low scorers.
marklistAnalysis.step1: Open Grading Reports and switch to the Marklist analysis tab.
marklistAnalysis.step2: Pick the semester, grade or section, then a subject — or keep Overall average for the combined view.
marklistAnalysis.step3: The performance ranges start from your grading scale; edit the min/max, add or remove ranges — the counts and chart re-bin instantly.
marklistAnalysis.step4: Review the distribution chart (male/female per range) and the top performers / low scorers lists.
marklistAnalysis.step5: The full ranked table below is searchable and filterable by gender, and exports to CSV or Excel.
marklistAnalysis.tip: Analysis reads the frozen results, so run Recompute on the report-cards page first if marks changed today.

submissionMonitor.title: Track marklist submissions
submissionMonitor.summary: See which teachers have not yet submitted their marklists and remind them with one tap.
submissionMonitor.step1: Open Grading reports under Academic and switch to the Submissions tab.
submissionMonitor.step2: The pipeline bar shows the whole semester at a glance: green is approved, amber is awaiting your approval, grey is still a draft and red has not been started. Tap a colour chip to filter the list to that state.
submissionMonitor.step3: Each row shows the teacher, the class, how much of the marks grid is already filled in, and when it was submitted. The list starts with the furthest-behind row.
submissionMonitor.step4: Press the bell on a row to send that teacher an in-app reminder listing their pending marklists, or "Remind all" to nudge everyone who is behind at once.
submissionMonitor.step5: Reminding again later refreshes the same notification instead of piling up new ones.
submissionMonitor.tip: The roster page shows a warning while marklists are still unapproved — the printed roster only matches report cards after everything is approved.

annualPlan.title: Build the annual plan (teachers)
annualPlan.summary: The year's roadmap for one subject and grade: goals, teaching load and the full unit grid.
annualPlan.step1: Open Lesson plans and press New annual plan — pick one of your classes (one plan covers all your sections of that subject and grade).
annualPlan.step2: Write the overall goals, the teaching methods, your periods per week and the total periods for the year.
annualPlan.step3: Add units: each chapter gets a title, objectives, why it matters, what students should already know, teaching aids, how learning is checked, textbook pages, a date window and a planned number of periods.
annualPlan.step4: You can also press Draft with AI on the Units tab: describe or paste the textbook chapters, review the suggested units, untick any you don't want, and add the rest in one tap — then set each unit's dates.
annualPlan.step5: The months and weeks on the printed sheet come from each unit's dates automatically — you never type them.
annualPlan.step6: Press Submit for review — the director or principal approves or declines it with a reason.
annualPlan.step7: Press Print official form any time for the paper sheet with signature lines, grouped by semester.
annualPlan.tip: Finalize the annual plan before classes start — daily lessons cannot be submitted until it is approved.

weeklyPlan.title: Daily lessons & the weekly submission (teachers)
weeklyPlan.summary: Daily lesson plans follow the standard school format; each week's set is submitted for review together.
weeklyPlan.step1: Write each day's lesson from My Day, or open the annual plan, tap a week on the rail and press Add lesson.
weeklyPlan.step2: A daily lesson carries the full format: topic and subtopic, why it matters, what students already know, objectives, the three stages (introduction, main activities, conclusion) with teacher and student activities, teaching aids and how learning is checked.
weeklyPlan.step3: Fill the support rows for students who need more help, most students, and fast finishers. Everything saves automatically as you type.
weeklyPlan.step4: Last week's uncovered lessons are offered as one-tap copies into this week.
weeklyPlan.step5: When the week's lessons are ready, press Submit week — if last week still has uncovered lessons you must explain the delay first.
weeklyPlan.step6: Each daily plan prints as the official form with signature lines.
weeklyPlan.tip: Link every lesson to its unit — that is how the platform proves your week matches the annual timeline.

coverage.title: Mark coverage after each class
coverage.summary: Record what was actually taught, per class — the delta drives carryover and pacing.
coverage.step1: Once the week is submitted, each sitting (class × period) takes its own mark.
coverage.step2: From My Day or the lesson itself, mark Covered, Partially covered or Not covered; add a note for anything missed.
coverage.step3: The same lesson can be covered in one section and missed in another — mark each one honestly.
coverage.step4: Use Copy to another day to move an unfinished lesson forward; its old sittings can be closed as not covered in the same step.
coverage.tip: Mark coverage right after class — an honest record is what justifies your pacing when the term gets disrupted.

reviewPlans.title: Review & approve plans (directors / principals)
reviewPlans.summary: The review inbox: approve or decline annual and weekly plans, with reasons on record.
reviewPlans.step1: Open Lesson plans → the Review tab. Submitted annual and weekly plans queue oldest first.
reviewPlans.step2: Open a plan to read it in full — units and timelines for annual plans, day-by-day lessons for weeks.
reviewPlans.step3: Weeks submitted behind schedule carry a Delay justified badge — read the teacher's reason before deciding.
reviewPlans.step4: Press Approve to countersign, or Decline with a written reason the teacher receives.
reviewPlans.step5: Reopen an approved plan when a legitimate change is needed — the history stays.
reviewPlans.tip: Decline reasons are the accountability trail: be specific about what must change.

pacing.title: The pacing dashboard
pacing.summary: Planned vs covered periods per teacher — who is on track and who needs support.
pacing.step1: Open Lesson plans → the Pacing tab.
pacing.step2: Each row is one approved plan: syllabus progress, periods behind, and the week trail (approved / declined / justified counts).
pacing.step3: Rows behind schedule glow amber — open one to see which unit is lagging.
pacing.step4: Use the record of unjustified delays and declines for performance conversations.
pacing.tip: Pacing compares coverage to the unit timeline pro-rated to today — a teacher mid-chapter is not counted behind.

myDay.title: My Day — plan straight from your timetable (teachers)
myDay.summary: Your real periods for the day, each showing its lesson plan or a one-tap way to write it.
myDay.step1: Open Lesson plans — the My Day tab shows your periods for today from the published timetable (swipe or use the arrows to change day).
myDay.step2: A period without a plan shows Plan this lesson — the subject, class, period and this week's unit are already filled in; you only type the topic.
myDay.step3: The full editor then opens for the lesson itself: objectives, the three teaching stages, support for different learners and homework.
myDay.step4: One lesson can serve all your parallel sections — add their sittings in the editor instead of writing it twice.
myDay.step5: After class, mark each sitting Covered, Partially covered or Not covered right from My Day.
myDay.tip: Plan tomorrow's lessons the evening before — everything is prefilled, so a lesson takes a few minutes.

bankAccounts.title: Set up payment accounts
bankAccounts.summary: Payment accounts are where families' money lands. Set them up before creating any fee.
bankAccounts.step1: Open Fees and go to payment accounts.
bankAccounts.step2: Pick the bank or wallet (Telebirr, CBE Birr, …) and enter the account number and holder name.
bankAccounts.step3: Accounts belong to the school; enable each one per branch.
bankAccounts.step4: Every fee then picks one or more collection accounts — where its payments can be recorded.
bankAccounts.tip: Payments remember the account they were made to. Re-pointing a fee later never rewrites past payments.

structures.title: Create fee structures
structures.summary: A fee structure describes a charge — school fees, transport, uniforms — for a year and set of grades.
structures.step1: Go to Fees and press the add button.
structures.step2: Pick the academic year, the grades it applies to (or all grades), the amount in ETB and the frequency — monthly, per semester, annual or one-time.
structures.step3: Set the start and due dates; optionally add penalties for late payment.
structures.step4: Choose one or more collection accounts payments can land in (e.g. Telebirr and CBE).
structures.step5: Turn on SMS notifications so parents and students are informed.
structures.step6: Flip on "Issue invoices now" to bill every enrolled student the moment the fee is saved — or leave it off and generate invoices later from the fee row.

invoices.title: Generate & manage invoices
invoices.summary: Invoices are the individual bills students owe.
invoices.step1: On a fee, press Generate invoices — every enrolled student in the applicable grades gets one.
invoices.step2: For a one-off charge, add a single invoice to one student from the Invoices page — optionally link it to a fee so it inherits the fee's collection accounts and standing discounts.
invoices.step3: Each invoice tracks its status: Unpaid, Partial or Paid.
invoices.step4: Filter and export the invoice list for follow-up calls and reports.
invoices.step5: Every invoice carries a number (e.g. INV-000123) — tap it to copy, and global search finds an invoice by its bare digits.
invoices.step6: The "Paid to" filter shows only invoices whose money landed in a chosen account — handy when reconciling a bank statement or the Telebirr wallet.

payments.title: Record payments
payments.summary: Record money as it arrives — in full or in parts.
payments.step1: Open an invoice and press Record payment.
payments.step2: Enter the amount and the receipt or transaction reference — the method (wallet, bank transfer, cash or other) follows from where the money landed.
payments.step3: Partial payments are fine: the balance is tracked until the invoice is paid.
payments.step4: The full payment history stays on the invoice.
payments.tip: Always capture the transaction reference — it's what settles disputes later.
payments.step5: Under "Where did the money land?", tap the account or wallet that received the money — the fee's own collection accounts are listed first, each with its logo and a tap-to-copy number. Cash and other need no account.

scholarships.title: Discounts & scholarships
scholarships.summary: A scholarship is recorded on the invoice itself — the history stays exact and reports still show the full amount.
scholarships.step1: On an invoice, choose Discount / scholarship.
scholarships.step2: Pick full scholarship (a reason is required), or a percentage/fixed discount for partial concessions.
scholarships.step3: The payable amount updates; payments are checked against the discounted amount.
scholarships.step4: Scholarships can also be granted during registration, on the fees step.
scholarships.tip: Never delete an invoice to make a fee free — grant a scholarship on it, so the record shows who was exempted and why.

accountReports.title: Payment accounts & reports
accountReports.summary: The Payment accounts page shows every collection account with how much it has collected, and a full report per account.
accountReports.step1: Open Payment accounts in the sidebar — each account shows total collected, transactions and the last payment date.
accountReports.step2: Use the switches to enable or disable an account for this branch or the whole school — you'll be asked to confirm.
accountReports.step3: Tap an account to open its report: monthly collection, breakdown by payment method and top fees.
accountReports.step4: The payments table below lists every payment into the account — filter by method and export it.
accountReports.tip: Accounts with payments can't be deleted — deactivate them instead, so history stays traceable.

concessions.title: Standing discounts & scholarships (concessions)
concessions.summary: A concession is a standing discount for a student — or a guardian's children — that applies automatically when new invoices are generated.
concessions.step1: Open Discounts in the sidebar and press Grant concession.
concessions.step2: Pick who it covers: one student, or a guardian (all their linked children).
concessions.step3: Choose the category (sibling, employee child, merit, hardship, scholarship), the discount (percentage, fixed or full scholarship) and which fees it touches.
concessions.step4: Scope it to one academic year or semester, or leave it lifetime until revoked.
concessions.step5: School policy can auto-suggest sibling and employee-child discounts (School settings) — suggestions wait in this page as Pending until finance approves or rejects them.
concessions.step6: Revoking a concession stops future bills only — invoices already issued keep their discount.
concessions.tip: New student with a discount? File the concession right inside the registration wizard (Enrollment & fees step) so the first invoice is already discounted — and when granting or approving one later, keep "Apply to open invoices" on to re-price bills issued moments earlier. Paid history is never touched.

invoiceDetails.title: Invoice details & payment review
invoiceDetails.summary: Every invoice opens into its full story — amounts, discounts, payments, and family payment submissions.
invoiceDetails.step1: Click any invoice row: a paid invoice opens its details (payments with transaction references, notes and who recorded them); an open one jumps straight to Record payment. Details are always available from the row menu → View details.
invoiceDetails.step2: The details sheet shows the money math — gross amount, any discount or concession, the payable amount, what was paid, and the balance. The invoice number is tap-to-copy everywhere it appears.
invoiceDetails.step3: When a family member submits a payment proof from the parent portal, the invoice shows a "Pending review" badge in the list — filter by it to see every claim waiting on finance.
invoiceDetails.step4: Open the invoice to review the submission: who sent it, the bank, transaction number, receipt, and what check.et read from bank records (amount, payer, receiving account). Duplicate transaction numbers are flagged in red. Press Confirm & record to post the payment, or Reject with a reason the family will see.
invoiceDetails.tip: Use the "Pending review" filter every morning — it is the queue of families who say they already paid.

notify.title: Send payment notices
notify.summary: Fee billed while notifications were off? Send the SMS/email notices on demand.
notify.step1: On the Fees page, open a fee's row menu and choose Send notifications.
notify.step2: Pick the audience: parents (every active guardian of a billed student) and/or students with their own account.
notify.step3: Review the confirmation — it shows exactly how many people will be reached, per channel (SMS and email), before anything goes out.
notify.step4: Confirm to send. Notices go only to students whose invoice for that fee is still unpaid or partially paid, in each recipient's own language.
notify.tip: Sending again later is safe — families with settled invoices are skipped automatically.

receipts.title: Print & verify receipts
receipts.summary: Every recorded payment gets an official numbered receipt with a QR code anyone can verify.
receipts.step1: Open the invoice, find the payment in its history and press Receipt.
receipts.step2: Print it — the number (RCT-…) comes from the branch's own sequence.
receipts.step3: The QR code opens a public verification copy straight from Temari.et — no login needed.
receipts.step4: If a paper receipt and the online copy disagree, trust the online copy.
receipts.tip: Families can scan the QR at any time — a doctored paper receipt is caught immediately.

recurringBilling.title: Monthly billing on autopilot
recurringBilling.summary: Monthly and quarterly fees can bill themselves — one invoice per Ethiopian month, per student.
recurringBilling.step1: Create a monthly (or quarterly) fee and flip on "Auto-issue each period's invoices".
recurringBilling.step2: Set the due day of the Ethiopian month (10 by default) — each month's invoice falls due on it.
recurringBilling.step3: Every day the engine bills any period that has started, for every actively enrolled student — including students who joined after the year began.
recurringBilling.step4: Students enrolling mid-year are only billed from their joining month; the school can choose to prorate the first month by days (Branch settings → Fees).
recurringBilling.step5: Prefer manual control? Leave auto-issue off and press Generate invoices on the fee — it back-fills every started month the same way.
recurringBilling.tip: Invoices are never duplicated: each student gets exactly one bill per fee per month, no matter how often generation runs.

reminders.title: Automatic payment reminders
reminders.summary: Families are reminded by SMS/email before a bill is due, on the due date, and while it stays unpaid.
reminders.step1: On the fee, turn on parent (and/or student) notifications — that's who the ladder writes to.
reminders.step2: Tune the ladder in Branch settings → Fees: days before due, how often to repeat once overdue, and when to stop.
reminders.step3: Reminders go out each morning automatically — no one has to press anything.
reminders.step4: Each rung is sent at most once per person per invoice, so nobody is spammed by re-runs.
reminders.tip: Reminders respect each guardian's channel preferences and the per-link SMS switch on the student's guardian record.

penalties.title: Late penalties
penalties.summary: Fees with a penalty rule accrue it automatically once an invoice is past due.
penalties.step1: On the fee, pick a penalty: fixed (one flat amount after the due date) or incremental (+amount every N days late).
penalties.step2: The system recomputes penalties daily; the invoice's balance always includes them.
penalties.step3: The invoice sheet shows the penalty as its own line — payments settle base + penalty.
penalties.step4: To forgive one, open the invoice and press Waive — the penalty is zeroed and never re-accrues.
penalties.tip: A full scholarship forgives any accrued penalty automatically.

feeReports.title: Fee reports
feeReports.summary: The receivables cockpit: what was billed, what came in, who owes, and how money arrived.
feeReports.step1: Open Fee reports from the sidebar (requires the reports permission).
feeReports.step2: Overview shows billed vs collected, the outstanding total, and the aging ladder — how long balances have been overdue.
feeReports.step3: Defaulters lists every student with an open balance, worst first, with guardian contacts for follow-up calls.
feeReports.step4: Collections shows day-by-day money in, split by payment method and by cashier.
feeReports.step5: Every table exports to CSV/Excel for the accountant.
feeReports.tip: Work the right side of the aging ladder first — the older a balance, the harder it is to collect.

books.title: Finance books (expenses & cashbook)
books.summary: Money out and non-fee money in, one dated cashbook, budgets and the income–expense statement.
books.step1: Open Finance books. First use provisions sensible Ethiopian categories — rename or add your own under Categories.
books.step2: Record expenses as they happen (rent, utilities, supplies…). Each stays Pending until a second person approves it. By default nobody approves their own expense; a school with a single finance person can allow self-approval in School settings → Finance controls.
books.step3: Record other income (hall rental, uniform sales, donations) under Other income.
books.step4: The Cashbook is a dated table of every birr in and out — fee payments, other income, approved expenses and payroll — grouped by day with daily totals. Search it, and filter by direction (money in / money out), source, category or payment method; the totals strip always matches your filters.
books.step5: The Statement sums income vs expenses by category for any period; payroll cost flows in automatically from approved payroll runs. Use Download PDF for a signed, QR-verified official copy.
