books.step6: Set a Budget per expense category for the year. The table shows spent, pending-approval, remaining and % used per category — over-budget rows turn red.
books.step7: A budget year counts approved expenses from its start until the day the NEXT year starts, so kremt (summer) spending is never lost between years. Pending expenses show separately and join the actuals once approved.
books.step8: Only principals and finance officers handle the books. Directors see fee status and reports but no money ledgers — unless the school enables Director finance access in School settings.
books.tip: If a budget shows 0% used, check two things: are the expenses still Pending approval, and are they dated inside the budget year's window (shown above the table)?

documents.title: Official PDFs & QR verification
documents.summary: Receipts, letters, transcripts, report cards, statements and payslips as fast, QR-verified PDFs.
documents.step1: Wherever you see Download PDF (receipt page, transfer/withdrawal letter, transcript, report card, statement, payslip), the platform serves a professionally formatted official PDF — no browser print dialogs.
documents.step2: Downloads are usually instant: documents are prepared ahead of time and cached. When one must be freshly generated you'll see “Generating — ready in a few seconds” and it downloads itself when done.
documents.step3: Every official PDF carries a QR code. Scanning it opens a public verification page proving the document is genuine — it shows who it was issued to and when, never marks or salaries. For receipts, letters and transcripts that page also hands you the same official PDF to download or print — never a printout of the web page.
documents.step4: When a payment is recorded, the family automatically receives the receipt link by SMS/email — they can view, verify and download the PDF without an account.
documents.step5: Issued a document by mistake? Revoke it — its QR immediately reports it as invalid, and a corrected copy gets a fresh code.
documents.tip: Anyone can verify a document — employers, universities, other schools — just by scanning the QR. No Temari.et account is needed.

inventory.title: Inventory & store
inventory.tagline: Items, stock, requests, purchase orders and counts

overview.title: What the inventory module is
overview.summary: One place for the school store: the item catalog, live stock per branch, staff requests, the optional purchase-order lane and physical counts.
overview.step1: Overview is home: the store's verbs as big buttons, what needs attention, and the latest activity. Items & stock lists everything with Low/Out badges against reorder levels.
overview.step2: Open any item to see its bin card — every receive, issue, return, adjustment and write-off with the running balance auditors expect — and, for assets, its tagged units.
overview.step3: Requests is where staff ask the store for items, approvers decide, and the storekeeper issues.
overview.step4: Requests, Purchase orders, Textbooks and Stock takes are the workflows; each lives in its own tab with its own approvals.
overview.tip: Stock is never edited directly. Every change is a ledger movement with a who, a when and a why — so the books always explain themselves.

requestItems.title: Request items from the store
requestItems.summary: Need chalk, paper or equipment? Ask the store from your phone and track the request to the moment it is handed over.
requestItems.step1: Open Inventory → Requests and tap "Request items".
requestItems.step2: Search the catalog and tap items to add them to your list; adjust quantities with the +/− steppers.
requestItems.step3: Add a short purpose so the approver knows what the items are for, then submit.
requestItems.step4: An approver decides your request — you are notified either way, with the reason if it was declined.
requestItems.step5: Once approved, the storekeeper issues the items. Collect them from the store; the request shows exactly what has been handed over so far.
requestItems.tip: You can edit or cancel your own request at any time before it is decided.

runTheStore.title: Run the store day to day
runTheStore.summary: The storekeeper's three verbs — receive, issue, count — all land in one append-only ledger.
runTheStore.step1: Add to store: one form creates the item AND its opening stock (or tagged units) together. Receive handles later deliveries — no purchase order needed.
runTheStore.step2: Issue: hand items out against an approved request, or directly — a direct issue always names who received it.
runTheStore.step3: Return brings unused items back to the shelf; Write-off removes damaged or expired stock with a required reason.
runTheStore.step4: Adjust corrects the count with a signed number (+ found surplus, − shrinkage) and a reason.
runTheStore.step5: Open any item to read its bin card: the full movement history with running balances, plus its tagged units if it is an asset.
runTheStore.step6: Set a reorder level on items you must never run out of — the store is alerted the moment stock crosses it.
runTheStore.tip: The ledger refuses to overdraw. If the app says there is not enough stock, count the shelf before forcing a correction.

approvals.title: Approve requests and orders
approvals.summary: Store requests and purchase orders are countersigned — the same four-eyes discipline as expenses.
approvals.step1: Pending requests and purchase orders reach you as notifications and sit under their tabs with a Pending badge.
approvals.step2: Open a request to trim quantities line by line before approving — approve 8 of the 10 boxes asked for.
approvals.step3: Declining always requires a reason; the requester reads it word for word.
approvals.step4: You can never decide your own request or order — a colleague must countersign.
approvals.tip: Approving reserves nothing. Stock only leaves the store when the storekeeper actually issues it.

purchaseOrders.title: Purchase orders (optional)
purchaseOrders.summary: When the school orders from a supplier, a purchase order tracks what was promised against what actually arrived.
purchaseOrders.step1: Purchase orders are optional — direct receiving always works. Use them when goods arrive later than the promise.
purchaseOrders.step2: Raise one with the supplier, the expected date and the ordered lines with unit costs; the total is computed for you.
purchaseOrders.step3: A colleague with approval authority countersigns it — never the person who raised it.
purchaseOrders.step4: As goods land, receive against the order — part deliveries are fine, and the order completes itself when every line arrives.
purchaseOrders.step5: Orders with nothing received yet can still be cancelled; once goods have landed, the history is permanent.
purchaseOrders.tip: Each receipt can carry the supplier's delivery-note number, so the paper trail and the ledger match.

stockTakes.title: Count the store (stock takes)
stockTakes.summary: A stock take compares the shelf against the books and posts the differences — the semester-end honesty check.
stockTakes.step1: Start a count from the Stock takes tab — the whole store, or one category at a time.
stockTakes.step2: Count with your phone: each line shows the expected quantity; type what you actually found. Save as you go.
stockTakes.step3: Lines you skip keep their current stock — the app never guesses zero for an uncounted shelf.
stockTakes.step4: Finishing posts each difference to the ledger as an adjustment against the LIVE balance, so stock that moved mid-count is never double-corrected.
stockTakes.step5: One count runs at a time per branch — post or cancel it before starting the next.
stockTakes.tip: Run one every semester. A store that is counted regularly is a store nobody quietly borrows from.

assetRegister.title: The asset register (tagged property)
assetRegister.summary: Every durable unit — projector, desk, microscope — gets a tag and a custody trail: who holds it, in what condition, since when.
assetRegister.step1: Flip the asset toggle when adding the item and its units are tagged in the same form — or open the item later and register more from there. Write each tag on the unit.
assetRegister.step2: Assign a unit to an employee, a student, a room or a section. One holder at a time — the register refuses double custody.
assetRegister.step3: Take units back with a condition (good, fair, damaged…) — the custody spell closes and the history stays.
assetRegister.step4: Send faulty units to repair and bring them back; mark vanished ones lost (custody closes automatically); dispose of dead ones — disposal is final.
assetRegister.step5: Filter the register by holder to answer the clearance question: "has this teacher returned everything?" — the offboarding checklist in one tap.
assetRegister.step6: Search any unit by its tag from anywhere — the ⌘K palette finds tags too.
assetRegister.tip: The register tracks identity; the stock ledger tracks quantity. Two books, like a property register and a bin card — that is deliberate.

textbooks.title: Textbook lending
textbooks.summary: Issue MoE textbooks to a whole section in one tap, collect them at year end, and record the ones that never come back.
textbooks.step1: Add each book title to the item catalog and receive the year's allocation into stock.
textbooks.step2: From the Textbooks tab, pick the year, the book and the section — every active student gets a copy, and students who already hold one are skipped automatically.
textbooks.step3: The whole issue lands on the ledger as ONE movement; each student gets a loan row their family can see in-app.
textbooks.step4: At year end, mark returns — per student or straight down the list. Returned copies go back into stock.
textbooks.step5: Mark missing copies lost: the family is notified, and the loan records it. No stock change — the copy left the shelf when it was issued.
textbooks.tip: Re-running an issue is always safe: current holders are skipped, so a half-finished distribution just continues where it stopped.

catalogs.title: Platform catalogs
catalogs.tagline: Curate the seed data every school uses

overview.title: What the catalogs are
overview.summary: Subjects, grade levels, banks, health conditions and the school directory are platform-owned reference data. Schools pick from them; the Temari.et team curates them.
overview.step1: Open Catalogs in the sidebar — the hub shows every catalog with live counts.
overview.step2: On desktop, hop between catalogs with the nested sidebar; on a phone, use the pill rail or the hub list.
overview.step3: An amber dot means something needs attention — usually unverified directory entries or inactive rows.
overview.step4: Every change is live for all schools immediately — there is no publish step.
overview.tip: Rows that schools already use (a bank with accounts, a condition on a student record) can only be deactivated, never deleted — history stays intact.

manageCatalog.title: Add or edit a catalog entry
manageCatalog.summary: Every catalog works the same way: search and filters at the top, a sheet form for add and edit, and a status switch to hide entries from school pickers.
manageCatalog.step1: Open the catalog and press the add button, or use a row's menu to edit.
manageCatalog.step2: Codes are stable machine keys (subject and bank codes) — set them once and avoid renaming.
manageCatalog.step3: For subjects, tick the exact grades it is taught in (gaps allowed — tap a cycle name to toggle the whole cycle; empty means every grade) and the room the subject needs; the semester grid and timetable use both.
manageCatalog.step4: Flip the status switch to hide an entry from schools without deleting it.
manageCatalog.step5: Use the export button to pull the filtered list as CSV or Excel.
manageCatalog.tip: School-custom subjects appear here for context but belong to their school — edit them from the school's own Subjects page.

gradeLadder.title: Edit the grade ladder
gradeLadder.summary: Grade levels (KG-1 … Grade 12) open as a spreadsheet: reorder by dragging, edit inline, and every change saves on its own — no sheet per row.
gradeLadder.step1: Open Grade levels. Each rung is a row, top to bottom in ladder order.
gradeLadder.step2: Drag a row by the handle on its left to move it; the whole ladder renumbers and saves at once.
gradeLadder.step3: Click the code or name cell and type to rename it — press Enter or click away to save.
gradeLadder.step4: Pick the cycle from the dropdown and flip the national-exam switch right in the row.
gradeLadder.step5: Use the delete icon to remove an unused rung, or the Add button for a new one.
gradeLadder.tip: Order anchors subject grade windows, so reordering shifts what each subject's grade range means — reorder deliberately.

reviewDirectory.title: Review the school directory
reviewDirectory.summary: Registrars add missing "previous schools" inline while enrolling students. Those rows arrive unverified and wait for platform review.
reviewDirectory.step1: Open School directory and filter by "Needs review".
reviewDirectory.step2: Check the name and location; fix typos with Edit — the row shows which school added it.
reviewDirectory.step3: Press Verify on good entries — verified rows rank first in every school's picker.
reviewDirectory.step4: Delete duplicates or junk; entries backed by a school on Temari are maintained automatically and cannot be deleted.
reviewDirectory.tip: Verifying promptly keeps the picker clean for every registrar in the country.

smsWhitelist.title: The SMS whitelist
smsWhitelist.summary: Every SMS costs money — decide which notification events may text.
smsWhitelist.step1: Open Catalogs → Notification events. Every alert the platform can emit is listed, grouped by topic.
smsWhitelist.step2: Each row has one switch: may this event send SMS? In-app and email behavior is fixed in code and costs nothing.
smsWhitelist.step3: Flip a switch to update the live whitelist instantly — every school on the platform follows it.
smsWhitelist.step4: Rows marked Critical (new sign-in, child absent, invoice due) should normally stay on — they are the safety net for parents without smartphones.
smsWhitelist.tip: Turning an event off never touches the in-app feed — users still see everything in the bell; only the paid text stops.

family.title: For families
family.tagline: Following your child, your account and preferences

parentPortal.title: Follow your children
parentPortal.summary: One account follows all your children — even at different schools.
parentPortal.step1: Sign in with your phone number; use the SMS link the school sent to set your password.
parentPortal.step2: Home shows the selected child at a glance: attendance, latest average, balance due and classwork — tap any tile to open the full page.
parentPortal.step3: Switch between children with the selector at the top.
parentPortal.step4: See fees and payment status when the school has enabled it for you.
parentPortal.step5: If a child is missing, ask their school to link you as a guardian — share your ID code.
parentPortal.tip: Your ID code (e.g. H8R6WV) is in Settings — any Temari.et school can find you with it.

attendance.title: Follow attendance day by day
attendance.summary: See each school day's status — and when your child checked in and out.
attendance.step1: Open Attendance from the sidebar. Parents with several children switch between them at the top.
attendance.step2: The header card shows the year's attendance ring, today's status with check-in and check-out times, the current streak and total absences.
attendance.step3: Every school day on the calendar is tinted by its status. Tap a status tile — Absent, for example — to spotlight those days in the month.
attendance.step4: Tap a day to see its check-in and check-out times, the Ethiopian date and any note the school added.
attendance.step5: Use the arrows — or swipe the calendar on a phone — to look at previous months.
attendance.tip: If your child is marked absent you get an SMS the same morning — check-out times are shown here in the app only.

transfers.title: Track and request school transfers
transfers.summary: Follow every school move for your children live, and apply to a new school online — no office queues.
transfers.step1: Open Transfers in the menu — every transfer involving your children is listed with its current stage.
transfers.step2: To request one, tap Request transfer, pick the child and find the new school.
transfers.step3: Write why you are moving and submit. Any unpaid fees are flagged first — the current school reviews them before approving.
transfers.step4: The new school responds first; if they accept, the request goes to the current school for final approval.
transfers.step5: You are notified by SMS at every step, and can withdraw the application any time before it is accepted.
transfers.tip: You will also get an SMS if any school files a transfer request for your child — so nothing ever moves without you knowing.

studentPortal.title: Your learning space
studentPortal.summary: Sign in with your phone or your student ID, and see your classes under Learning.
studentPortal.step1: Sign in with your phone number — or, if you don't have a phone, with your 6-character student ID (it's on your ID card) and your PIN.
studentPortal.step2: If your ID card has a QR code, scanning it opens the sign-in page with your ID already filled — just type your PIN.
studentPortal.step3: Forgot your PIN? Use "Forgot PIN?" on the sign-in page. The reset code goes to your phone, or to your parent's phone if you don't have one.
studentPortal.step4: Home greets you with today's classes and due work; Results, Attendance, Timetable and Calendar are one tap away in the sidebar.

preferences.title: Language & notifications
preferences.summary: Choose the language you read and how the school may reach you.
preferences.step2: Pick English, አማርኛ or Afaan Oromoo — SMS from the school arrives in the same language.
preferences.step3: Turn SMS, email or push notifications on or off.

verifyPayment.title: Submit a payment
verifyPayment.summary: Pay at the bank or wallet as usual, then submit the proof in the app — no queuing at the school.
verifyPayment.step1: Open Payments and pick the child. Each invoice shows its number, due date and the exact school accounts to pay into — tap a bank logo to copy the account number.
verifyPayment.step2: Press Submit payment on the fee you paid, then choose how to prove it: bank + transaction number (best), a receipt share-link, or an uploaded PDF/screenshot. On a computer you can drag the file straight onto the upload box.
verifyPayment.step3: The payment is checked against bank records instantly — verified payments settle the fee on the spot.
verifyPayment.step4: If something needs a human look (unusual amount or account), it shows as "awaiting confirmation" and the school finance office sees it on the invoice and confirms it.
verifyPayment.step5: Each receipt can be used only once — reused receipts are rejected automatically.
verifyPayment.tip: The transaction number on your receipt or confirmation SMS is the fastest way — it works even without a smartphone screenshot.

feeReminders.title: Payment reminders & receipts
feeReminders.summary: What the school-fee SMS messages mean and how to check a receipt.
feeReminders.step1: You may get an SMS/email a few days before a fee is due, on the due day, and occasionally while it stays unpaid — pay at the school or submit your payment in the app.
feeReminders.step2: In Payments you can see each bill's amount, any late penalty, what is already paid and the remaining balance.
feeReminders.step3: Every payment has an official receipt; scan the QR code on a printed receipt to verify it is genuine.
feeReminders.tip: You control channels under Preferences — turn SMS or email on or off any time.

classwork.title: Submit homework & take exams
classwork.summary: Classwork is the student's home for assignments, exams and study materials.
classwork.step1: Assignments, Exams and Materials each have their own page in the sidebar — Home also shows what is due soon and which exams are open.
classwork.step2: Open an assignment, write your answer (you can format it and add pictures) or attach files — rename them so your teacher knows what they are — and press Submit before the deadline.
classwork.step3: Some homework is a quiz. Open it and answer inside the exam player — it is turned in automatically when you submit the quiz, so there is no separate Submit button. A finished quiz shows a “Completed” mark (with your score) instead of Submit.
classwork.step4: To sit an exam press Start. Supervised exams ask for the code your teacher shares in the room.
classwork.step5: Answers save automatically as you go — if the connection drops, nothing is lost; continue where you left off.
classwork.step6: When results are released you see your score, and where the teacher allows it, the correct answers with explanations.
classwork.tip: Stay on the exam screen: leaving it, copying or pasting is recorded and shown to your teacher.

classPlan.title: Follow the class plan
classPlan.summary: See each subject's syllabus roadmap and what is planned this week.
classPlan.step1: Open Class plan from the menu (parents: pick the child first).
classPlan.step2: Each subject card shows the teacher, syllabus progress and the chapter roadmap.
classPlan.step3: Expand a subject to see this week's approved topics and homework, marked as they are covered.
classPlan.step4: Only teacher plans approved by the school appear here.
classPlan.tip: Check the plan on Monday — homework for the week is usually listed on it.

childLearning.title: Follow your child's classwork
childLearning.summary: See homework status and exam results for each linked child.
childLearning.step1: Open Learning under My family and pick the child.
childLearning.step2: Assignments show what was submitted, what is late and what is still missing.
childLearning.step3: Scores appear when the school has allowed grade visibility on your guardian link.

takeCourses.title: Take a course
takeCourses.summary: Courses from your school and Temari's exam-prep catalog live under Courses, with your progress saved.
takeCourses.step1: Open Courses — each card shows a progress bar and a Continue button that returns you to where you stopped.
takeCourses.step2: Work through lessons: watch videos, read notes, download files, and sit quiz checkpoints in the exam player.
takeCourses.step3: Tap "Mark complete" when you finish a lesson — quiz lessons complete automatically when you submit the quiz.
takeCourses.step4: In sequential courses lessons unlock in order; finish the earlier ones to open the next.
takeCourses.tip: Videos load only when you tap play, so browsing courses costs almost no data.

results.title: Follow marks & results
results.summary: Results shows live marks as teachers record them, plus report cards and the transcript.
results.step1: Open Results from the sidebar. Parents pick a child at the top.
results.step2: The Marks tab lists every subject — tap one to see each test and its score. A "Signed off" badge means the teacher submitted the marklist; other scores are still provisional.
results.step3: The Report cards tab holds every released semester report — open one to view or print it.
results.step4: The Transcript tab summarises each academic year; open the full transcript for the official record.
results.tip: Scores appear as soon as teachers record them — check during the semester, not only at report time.

absenceExcuse.title: Excuse an absence
absenceExcuse.summary: If your child was absent for a good reason, file an excuse for the school to review.
absenceExcuse.step1: Open Attendance and scroll to Absence excuses, then press Request excuse.
absenceExcuse.step2: Pick the day(s), explain the reason, and attach proof if you have it — a medical note helps.
absenceExcuse.step3: The request lands with the school as Pending — you are notified when it is decided.
absenceExcuse.step4: If approved, the absent days change to Excused on the attendance calendar.
absenceExcuse.tip: File the excuse as soon as your child returns — approved excuses keep the record clean.

paymentsHub.title: Fees: due, upcoming & receipts
paymentsHub.summary: Payments shows what is due now, what is coming, and every receipt.
paymentsHub.step1: Open Payments. The Due tab lists open invoices with the school's collection accounts — tap an invoice to submit a payment for verification.
paymentsHub.step2: The Upcoming tab previews the next monthly fees before they are billed, so you can plan ahead.
paymentsHub.step3: The History tab lists every recorded payment — tap the receipt icon to open the official QR receipt.
paymentsHub.step4: The strip at the top totals the outstanding balance; a red badge counts overdue invoices.
paymentsHub.tip: Receipts never expire — re-open and share them any time.

calendar.title: The school calendar
calendar.summary: One agenda of holidays, exams, assessments and homework deadlines.
calendar.step1: Open Calendar from the sidebar. Parents pick a child at the top.
calendar.step2: The next three months are grouped by day — holidays, semester start and end, planned tests, exam windows and assignment deadlines.
calendar.step3: The Today marker shows where you are; new events appear as the school plans them.
calendar.tip: Exam dates appear as soon as teachers schedule them — a weekly glance keeps surprises away.

hireTutor.title: Hire a private tutor
hireTutor.summary: Verified tutors for every grade and subject — you pay Temari.et monthly, and the tutor is paid only after the lessons are confirmed.
hireTutor.step1: Open Tutoring → Find a tutor and browse the directory (filter by subject, city, price and rating).
hireTutor.step2: Open a profile and press Request this tutor — choose the child (or yourself), subjects and how many sessions per week.
hireTutor.step3: The tutor accepts (or declines) your request; you are notified either way.
hireTutor.step4: Pay the first month — sessions can start the moment the month is paid.
hireTutor.step5: Chat with the tutor in Messages to agree days and times.
hireTutor.tip: The monthly estimate on the request form shows exactly what a month costs before you commit.

tutorPayments.title: Tutoring payments & confirmations
tutorPayments.summary: Your money sits safely with Temari.et until the lessons actually happen.
tutorPayments.step1: Open Tutoring — months waiting for payment are at the top; pay with any available method.
tutorPayments.step2: After each lesson the tutor logs it — confirm it within 72 hours (or raise an issue if it did not happen).
tutorPayments.step3: At month end, only confirmed lessons are paid to the tutor; anything unfulfilled becomes credit on your next month.
tutorPayments.step4: After a completed month, rate your tutor — reviews keep the directory honest.
tutorPayments.tip: Never pay a tutor outside the app — outside payments have no escrow protection.

firstSetup.title: First-time setup (guided)
firstSetup.summary: The first time you open Timetable for a semester, a three-step wizard walks you through everything the schedule needs — you cannot get lost.
firstSetup.step1: Step 1 — School day: generate the standard Ethiopian day (classes, breaks, lunch) with one tap, then adjust times. This is required; lessons hang on these period numbers.
firstSetup.step2: Step 2 — Rooms (optional): add only the rooms sections share, like labs, ICT and the gym. Skip it if you have none; you can add rooms later.
firstSetup.step3: Step 3 — Timetable: name your first draft, choose whether Saturday is a school day, and create it.
firstSetup.step4: You land on the grid — press Generate to fill it automatically, adjust, then publish.
firstSetup.tip: Prefer the classic tabs? Press "Set up manually" at the top of the wizard. The wizard only appears while the semester has no timetable versions.

periodSchedule.title: Set up the period schedule
periodSchedule.summary: The period schedule is the day’s skeleton: teaching periods, breaks and lunch. Lessons point at period numbers, so changing a time here re-times the whole timetable at once.
periodSchedule.step1: Open Timetable and switch to the Period schedule tab.
periodSchedule.step2: Press Generate default — you get the standard day: 3 classes, a 15-minute break, 2 classes, another break, lunch (45 min), then 3 closing classes.
periodSchedule.step3: Adjust times, add or remove blocks (class, break, lunch, flag ceremony). Change a block's end time and the next block starts exactly there — the rest of the day shifts with it, so you never re-type the times below. Deleting a block closes its gap the same way.
periodSchedule.step4: Save. Every existing lesson instantly follows the new times.
periodSchedule.tip: Class periods are numbered automatically from their order — a lesson in "Period 3" stays Period 3 even if you shift the whole morning.

build.title: Generate and tune the schedule
build.summary: Create a draft, let the generator place every lesson under the rules (no clashes, teacher availability, heavy subjects in the morning), then fine-tune by hand.
build.step1: Make sure the semester's teaching grid (subjects × sections × teachers with periods per week) is complete.
build.step2: Press New draft, name it, and choose whether Saturday is a school day. Generate the schedule for me now is ticked by default — the grid is filled automatically the moment the draft is created. Untick it to start from an empty grid and place lessons yourself.
build.step3: If you left it ticked, the filled grid arrives in seconds; otherwise press Generate. Either way the system reports anything it could not place.
build.step4: Review section by section. Tap a lesson to move, lock or remove it; tap a lesson from the To place tray, then tap a free cell.
build.step5: Lock the lessons that must not move, then press Regenerate unlocked to let the solver rearrange the rest.
build.step6: Conflicting placements are refused on the spot with the reason (teacher busy, section busy, room taken).
build.tip: Add your labs, gym and ICT rooms under Rooms first — subjects that need one (Chemistry, Physics, HPE, IT) get a free room booked automatically during generation; when every room is taken the lesson falls back to the section's own classroom.

publish.title: Publish the timetable
publish.summary: Publishing makes the timetable visible to teachers, students and parents. The previous published version is archived, never lost.
publish.step1: Open the draft and press Publish — the system audits it for conflicts first.
publish.step2: Teachers see their own weekly schedule; families see it on the child's page.
publish.step3: For a mid-term fix (teacher left, room closed), edit the published grid directly — every change is validated.
publish.tip: Keep the old version archived instead of deleting it — it is the record of what the school actually ran.

promotion.title: Promotion & year-end

board.title: Decide promotions on the board
board.summary: The promotion board lists every student of the year with semester averages, attendance and a policy suggestion, and rows are tinted by their decision. You decide; nothing moves until the rollover.
board.step1: Close the semesters first — averages and ranks freeze when a semester closes.
board.step2: Open Promotion — the board starts on the first grade that has sections. Switch grade or section, or use the filters (average, attendance, suggestion, decision) to focus the list.
board.step3: Check the pass mark: editing it re-scores suggestions and colors live. It is a preview only — tick “Update branch default too” to also save it as the branch setting.
board.step4: Press Accept suggestions to fill in the policy defaults: promote at or above the pass mark, repeat below it, graduate the top grade.
board.step5: Override any student's decision and add a note explaining why.
board.step6: Press Save decisions. You can return and change them any time before the rollover.
board.tip: Students awaiting national exam results (Grade 6/8/12) can simply stay undecided until the results arrive.

rollover.title: Run the year rollover
rollover.summary: The rollover executes saved decisions one student at a time: promoted students move up a grade, repeaters stay, graduates close their file. It is safe to re-run.
rollover.step1: Create the next academic year first (it can stay in planned status).
rollover.step2: On the promotion board press Run rollover and pick the target year.
rollover.step3: Promoted students land one grade up — same section letter when it exists and has room, otherwise the section-assignment pool.
rollover.step4: New enrollments start pending until the registration fee is paid or covered by a scholarship (per school policy).
rollover.step5: Review the result: moved count plus a list of any skipped students with reasons.
rollover.tip: Run grade by grade if you prefer — pass a grade filter and only those decisions execute.

revert.title: Revert a promotion made by mistake
revert.summary: Ran the rollover too early, or promoted the wrong students? Revert moves them back safely: the new year's enrollment is removed, its unpaid bills are cancelled, and each student returns to their previous grade and section.
revert.step1: For one student: find the row on the promotion board and press the revert (↩) button on it.
revert.step2: For a whole batch: with a grade selected (or all grades), press Revert in the bottom bar — every executed decision in view moves back.
revert.step3: The saved decision is kept as "decided" — correct it if needed and run the rollover again for exactly those students.
revert.step4: Students who already have attendance, marks or a received payment in the new year are skipped and listed with the reason — those need a person to review them first.
revert.tip: If a family already paid for the new year, refund or void that payment in Finance first — the revert never touches money silently.

promotion.tagline: Year-end results, decisions and the rollover

request.title: Request a student from another school
request.summary: When a family arrives from another Temari school, no paperwork is needed: request the student by their ID and the current school approves digitally.
request.step1: Ask the family for the student ID (on the report card and the Temari app).
request.step2: Open Transfers → New transfer request and enter the ID — you see the student's name, school and grade only.
request.step3: Choose the academic year and grade they will join, and write the reason.
request.step4: Attach supporting documents — report card, fee-clearance slip, parent's letter — up to 5 files; the current school reviews them before deciding.
request.step5: Send the request. The current school is notified and reviews it.
request.step6: On approval the student instantly belongs to your school — history intact, transfer letter printable.
request.tip: Students from schools OUTSIDE Temari are registered through the normal wizard with their paper transfer letter scanned into documents.

decide.title: Approve or reject an incoming request
decide.summary: Approval is the handover: the enrollment closes at your school and opens at the receiving one, in a single safe step. Rejection sends your reason back.
decide.step1: Open Transfers → Incoming — requests for your students appear here.
decide.step2: Check the student's file first, especially outstanding fees.
decide.step3: Any supporting documents the requesting school attached open right inside the approve/reject dialog.
decide.step4: Approve to hand over, or Reject with a note (e.g. unpaid balance).
decide.step5: After approval both schools can print the transfer letter.
decide.tip: Approval cannot be undone — the receiving school would have to transfer the student back.

applications.title: Handle online transfer applications
applications.summary: Families can apply to your school straight from their Temari.et portal. You see a limited profile only; accepting turns the application into a normal transfer request that the student's current school approves.
applications.step1: Open Transfers → Applications — every family application addressed to your school is listed.
applications.step2: Review the student's name, current school and grade, the applicant and their reason.
applications.step3: To accept, choose the academic year and the grade you are placing the student into.
applications.step4: Accepting sends a standard transfer request to the student's current school — they keep the final say (and check fee clearance).
applications.step5: To decline, write a short note — the family sees it in their portal.
applications.tip: You only see directory-level facts until the current school approves. The full record arrives with the handover.

withdraw.title: Withdraw a student (leaving school)
withdraw.summary: When a family leaves Temari entirely or moves to a school outside the platform, withdraw the enrollment and print the QR-verified clearance letter. Records are never deleted.
withdraw.step1: Open Students, find the student and choose Withdraw student from the row menu.
withdraw.step2: The dialog shows any outstanding balance up-front — fees never block a withdrawal; the amount is noted on the letter instead.
withdraw.step3: Write the reason, optionally the destination school, and confirm the date.
withdraw.step4: Confirm. The enrollment closes, the seat is freed, and the family is notified by SMS.
withdraw.step5: Print the clearance letter from the toast (or later via the enrollment) — its QR code lets any school verify it online.
withdraw.tip: Moving to another TEMARI school? Use a transfer instead — the receiving school requests, you approve, and the history stays connected.

letter.title: The transfer letter and its QR code
letter.summary: Every approved transfer produces a printable letter with a QR code. Scanning the code opens a public copy of the letter on Temari, so anyone can verify it is genuine.
letter.step1: Open Transfers and choose Transfer letter on an approved request.
letter.step2: Print the letter — the QR code prints with it.
letter.step3: Anyone who scans the code sees the verified letter online; a forged or altered letter will not match.
letter.tip: The QR link works without a Temari account — parents and other schools can use it.

afterTransfer.title: What your school keeps after a student leaves
afterTransfer.summary: When a student transfers away, your school keeps a read-only copy of the file exactly as it was on the day of the handover — documents, health data, guardians, address — plus everything your school produced. Nothing the new school adds afterwards is visible to you.
afterTransfer.step1: The student stays on your register with a "Transferred out" badge — open the profile to see the frozen file: documents, health data, guardians and address as they were at departure, plus your enrollment history, results and fee ledger.
afterTransfer.step2: Editing is closed: the record now belongs to the new school. Anything they change or add after the handover never appears in your copy.
afterTransfer.step3: Documents travel with the student — the new school receives everything your school collected, and your copy of those files stays visible to you.
afterTransfer.step4: Transfer paperwork is never lost: the supporting files of every transfer your school took part in stay on the student's Documents tab, and your report cards, transcripts and receipts remain printable forever.
afterTransfer.tip: If the student ever transfers back, your school regains the full live record automatically — including everything collected elsewhere in between.

questionBanks.title: Build a question bank
questionBanks.summary: Banks are organized subject → grade → chapters. Build them once, reuse them every term.
questionBanks.step1: Go to Question banks and create a bank — pick the subject and grade, then type its chapters (e.g. Algebra, Geometry).
questionBanks.step2: Add questions in the full-screen editor: write the question with formatting and images, attach links, videos or files, and pick the answer type.
questionBanks.step3: Mark the correct answer(s) as you write, and add an explanation — students see it after grading and learn from it.
questionBanks.step4: In the side panel set points, difficulty and the chapter, then Save & publish — or save as a draft and publish later; drafts never appear in exams.
questionBanks.step5: Press Preview — on the bank page or from the eye button on the banks list — to page through the questions exactly as a student will see them and catch formatting slips early. Directors and principals see every bank in the branch; teachers manage the banks they created.
questionBanks.tip: Questions used in an exam are never deleted — they retire instead, so past results always stay intact.

richQuestions.title: Formulas, images and passage questions
richQuestions.summary: Write textbook-grade questions: mathematical formulas and images in the question AND in the answer choices, plus reading passages that bundle several questions into one unit.
richQuestions.step1: In the question editor press the Σ button — an equation picker opens, like in Word or Google Docs. Tap structures (fraction, root, integral, sum…) and symbols (Greek letters, operators, arrows) to build the formula; the live preview updates as you go. Advanced users can type LaTeX directly. Press “Own line” for a centered display formula, and click any inserted formula to edit it.
richQuestions.step2: Answer choices have their own mini editor — bold, sub/superscript, formulas and images all work inside a choice, so options like x² or a diagram are first-class.
richQuestions.step3: For a reading passage, create a question of type “Question group (passage)”. Write the full passage as its text — with images and formatting.
richQuestions.step4: Add its questions right inside the editor: the “Questions in this passage” card lists them with an Add sub-question button — each opens the normal question editor with its own type, points and answer. A passage can mix types freely; reorder with the arrows or press Group by type to arrange them in the customary paper order, edit or remove them from the same list, and use the eye button to preview the passage exactly as students will see it.
richQuestions.step5: In the bank the passage is ONE row showing its question count and total marks — its questions never appear as separate rows. On an exam, pick the passage once: every question joins together and shuffling never separates them.
richQuestions.tip: Formulas are stored as LaTeX and rendered everywhere — the exam player, results, the printed A4 paper and the marking key.

createExam.title: Create and publish an exam
createExam.summary: Quizzes and exams run online across one or many sections, grade themselves where possible, and can feed the marklist automatically.
createExam.step1: Go to Exams & quizzes and press New exam. In the full-screen editor pick the grade, the subject, then every section that sits this paper.
createExam.step2: Write the title and instructions (formatting and images supported) — students see them on the cover page before starting. Then pick the paper: fixed questions from a bank, or random-draw rules.
createExam.step3: In the side panel set the time limit, the open/close window and how many attempts are allowed.
createExam.step4: For supervised exams set an access code — reveal it in the exam room, so only students present can start.
createExam.step5: To make it count toward grades, pick the continuous-assessment slot — each section's marks land in its own gradebook. Use Preview to page through the exam exactly as a student will.
createExam.step6: Press Save & publish (or keep it as a draft). The exam page shows how many of the expected students have taken it — the same completion rate appears on the exams list.
createExam.tip: Shuffle questions and choices — neighbours get different papers, which beats any camera.

paperParts.title: Group questions into parts and print the paper
paperParts.summary: Organise an exam like a real paper — Part I Multiple Choice, Part II True or False… — and print it as a clean A4 PDF for the classroom.
paperParts.step1: In the exam editor pick your questions, then press Add part. Give the part a title (e.g. Multiple Choice) and, optionally, its own instructions (e.g. “Choose the best answer”).
paperParts.step2: Drag a question onto a part to file it there, or use the small folder menu on each question row on mobile. Drag between parts to move; the chevrons nudge a question up or down within its part.
paperParts.step3: Press Group by type to build the whole structure in one click — a part per question type, in the customary order, with ready-made titles and instructions you can edit.
paperParts.step4: Questions left outside a part appear under Unassigned and come after the last part. Question numbering runs continuously across the whole paper.
paperParts.step5: Students see each part’s title and instructions while writing, and shuffling never moves a question out of its part — exactly like a printed paper.
paperParts.step6: To use the exam on paper, open the exam page and press Print: the question paper is a print-ready A4 PDF with a candidate box, part headers, answer lines and marks. Managers can also print the Answer key.
paperParts.tip: The printed paper and the online exam are the same source of truth — edit the exam once and reprint; unchanged papers re-serve instantly.

monitorGrading.title: Monitor attempts and grade
monitorGrading.summary: Watch the exam live, review flagged sittings and grade the answers that need a human.
monitorGrading.step1: Open the exam — every attempt appears live with its status and score.
monitorGrading.step2: Flags count suspicious moments (leaving the screen, pasting, another device). Review them before judging — a flaky connection also leaves flags.
monitorGrading.step3: Attempts with essays or unmatched short answers wait in "Needs grading" — open one and score each answer with feedback.
monitorGrading.step4: Results reach students per the exam's reveal policy: immediately, after close, or when you release them.
monitorGrading.step5: An unfair sitting can be invalidated — it stops counting and the student gets their attempt back.
monitorGrading.tip: The clock is on the server: closing the app or losing connection never gains a student extra time.

homework.title: Post and grade homework
homework.summary: Assignments reach students online; submissions land in one grading queue.
homework.step1: Go to Assignments and press New assignment — the full-screen editor opens. Pick the grade, the subject, then the section.
homework.step2: Write the title and rich instructions (formatting, images, video links). Choose how students submit: written answer, files, a photo of paper work, audio, or a link.
homework.step3: In the right rail set when the work opens and when it is due — the due date and time must come after the start — plus the late policy (accept with an optional penalty, or refuse) and the status: Save & publish now or keep it as a draft.
homework.step4: Attach worksheets or readings — PDF, Word or LibreOffice documents, slides, spreadsheets and CSV data, plain text, pictures, audio, video or a zip, up to 20 MB each. Students preview them right inside the app.
homework.step5: Grade from the submissions queue: read, score, write feedback. Linked assignments push scores to the marklist.
homework.tip: Students can improve their submission until you grade it — after that it is frozen.

materials.title: Share learning materials
materials.summary: Notes, files, videos and links — posted once, visible to the right classes.
materials.step1: Go to Materials and press Post material.
materials.step2: Pick the type: a file (PDF, slides…), a link, a YouTube video or a written note.
materials.step3: Teachers pick which of their classes see it; directors can share by grade for the whole branch.
materials.step4: Pin the important ones — pinned materials stay on top for students.
materials.tip: Videos play inside the app via YouTube — students only load the video when they tap play, saving data.

assignmentKinds.title: Assignment types, rubrics and targeting
assignmentKinds.summary: Assignments come in two kinds — standard and quiz — with rubrics, resubmission rules and per-student targeting.
assignmentKinds.step1: Pick the kind when you create an assignment: Standard (students turn work in) or Quiz (a quiz from your class IS the work — attempts grade automatically, and students enter its access code if it has one).
assignmentKinds.step2: For standard work, choose what students may submit: written answers, files, a photo of paper work, an audio recording, or a link.
assignmentKinds.step3: Grade with a rubric when the mark has parts: add criteria with points — their sum becomes the total, and you score line by line.
assignmentKinds.step4: Set the resubmission policy (until graded / once / single submission) and a late policy with an optional automatic percentage penalty.
assignmentKinds.step5: Untick "Whole class" to assign remedial or extension work to specific students only — nobody else sees it.
assignmentKinds.tip: Each assignment carries a private message thread per student — the students table shows a Messages pill per row (even before a submission), and the grading screen has the chat beside the work.

courses.title: Build a course (modules and lessons)
courses.summary: Courses are structured self-study: ordered modules holding video, reading, file and quiz lessons, with per-student progress — built in one full-screen studio.
courses.step1: Go to Courses → New course. In the side panel, pick the subject, then the grades and sections that take it (your only subject is pre-selected; on phones, tap the audience bar under the title bar). Name the course — from that moment it autosaves as a draft.
courses.step2: Teachers target their own classes — several sections can take one course; Temari staff publish platform prep courses with a grade window, and a stream choice appears only when the window reaches grade 11–12.
courses.step3: Build the structure right in the studio: add modules (units/chapters), then tap Add lesson — a full-screen lesson editor opens for a YouTube/MP4 video, a rich-text reading (images, links, video embeds), a downloadable file, or a quiz checkpoint.
courses.step4: Quiz lessons reuse your existing quizzes — students complete the lesson by actually sitting the quiz, never by just tapping done.
courses.step5: Turn on Sequential to lock lessons in order — students must finish one to open the next.
courses.step6: Finish with Save & publish (or keep it a draft; the status control in the side rail also re-drafts or archives). Students only ever see published courses.
courses.tip: A course with learner progress archives instead of deleting — nobody's progress is ever lost.

chat.title: Messages & chat
chat.tagline: Talking to staff, families and your whole school community

basics.title: Send and receive messages
basics.summary: One inbox for direct messages, groups and school channels.
basics.step1: Open Messages from the sidebar (or the bottom bar on your phone).
basics.step2: Tap the pencil button to start a new conversation, or pick an existing one from the list.
basics.step3: Write your message and press send. Long-press or hover a message to reply, react with an emoji, or edit it within 15 minutes.
basics.step4: Mention a person in a group with @ and their name — they get their own notification even if they muted the group.
basics.step5: Use the search bar to find any conversation or old message.
basics.tip: Pin the conversations you use daily from the details panel — they stay on top. Mute noisy groups; mentions still reach you.

familyChat.title: Message a student's family
familyChat.summary: Family conversations are anchored to the student, never to one phone number.
familyChat.step1: Start a new message and open the Families tab.
familyChat.step2: Pick the student — the conversation opens with all of the child's guardians at once.
familyChat.step3: Teachers only see their own students; the school office can reach any family in the branch.
familyChat.step4: Parents can also start the conversation from their side: they see their child's teachers, homeroom teacher and school office.
familyChat.step5: Parents never see or message other parents — family privacy is built in.
familyChat.step6: Even faster: on the Students, Parents and Employees pages, use the chat icon on a row — or tap any phone number and choose Message. The conversation opens right there, without leaving the page.
familyChat.tip: If the school gate is on, your message to a family first goes to the director for approval — you will see "waiting for approval" under it.

communicationBook.title: The communication book (approvals)
communicationBook.summary: Directors review teacher messages to families before the family sees them.
communicationBook.step1: When the school gate is on, teacher messages to families are held for review — either every message, or only the first message of each conversation (set in School settings).
communicationBook.step2: Directors get a notification and see the pending count above their conversation list — tap it to open the communication book.
communicationBook.step3: Approve to deliver the message to the family instantly.
communicationBook.step4: Return a message with a short note when it needs rephrasing — the family never sees returned messages.
communicationBook.step5: The setting lives in School settings, and each branch can override it in Branch settings.
communicationBook.tip: Directors can also open any teacher–family conversation read-only for oversight. Every such view is recorded in the activity log.

messageTemplates.title: Preset message templates
messageTemplates.summary: School-curated messages teachers send with one tap — delivered in the family’s own language.
messageTemplates.step1: Directors and principals open Messages and tap the template icon at the top to manage the library.
messageTemplates.step2: Create a template: pick a category (attendance, homework, praise…), write the message in English, Amharic and Afan Oromo, and use placeholders like {student_name} — they fill in automatically.
messageTemplates.step3: Teachers tap the template icon in the chat composer: presets appear already translated into the family’s language with the child’s name filled in. One tap inserts the text.
messageTemplates.step4: In school settings (Chat tab) choose the mode: Suggested (teachers may also write freely) or Required (messages to families must use a template).
messageTemplates.step5: School-wide templates serve every branch; a branch can add its own next to them, and each branch can override the mode.
messageTemplates.tip: Templates work together with the communication book — a preset message still goes through approval where the school requires it.

channels.title: Channels and announcements
channels.summary: Staff rooms, classroom groups and announcement channels are created for you.
channels.step1: Every branch gets a Staff room (all staff can post) and an Announcements channel (leadership posts, everyone reads).
channels.step2: Every class gets a classroom group with its teachers and parents — membership follows enrollment automatically.
channels.step3: Directors and principals can create custom channels or send a mass message: turn on Staff and/or Families, then narrow it — staff by role, families by grade and by class. Leave a scope open to reach everyone in it.
channels.step4: React to announcements with an emoji — it is the lightest way to say "seen".
channels.step5: Anything can also go out by SMS, not only emergencies — flip the “Also send by SMS” switch under the composer to text everyone in the channel. If your post has a photo or file, the SMS carries a link to open it.
channels.step6: Open the channel’s info sheet any time to see exactly who it reaches — the roles, grades and classes it was aimed at.
channels.tip: Students join classroom groups only when the school enables student chat in settings — it is off by default.

voiceAndFiles.title: Voice notes and files
voiceAndFiles.summary: Send photos, documents and voice messages on any connection.
voiceAndFiles.step1: Tap the paperclip to attach photos or documents — rename each file before sending so the other side knows what it is.
voiceAndFiles.step2: With an empty message box, tap the microphone to record a voice note; tap the square to send it.
voiceAndFiles.step3: Images show as previews; documents open with one tap.
voiceAndFiles.step4: On a slow connection messages retry safely — you will never send a duplicate.
voiceAndFiles.tip: Voice notes are perfect for quick updates to parents who prefer listening over reading.

practice.title: Practice for national exams
practice.summary: Free mock exams and past papers for Grade 6, 8 and 12 — for every Temari user, with or without a school.
practice.step1: Open Exam prep from the menu — no school account is needed, any signed-in user can practice.
practice.step2: Filter by your grade and subject to find mock exams and past papers.
practice.step3: Start a mock — it runs like a real exam, with a timer and one question per screen.
practice.step4: Submit to see your score immediately, with the correct answers and explanations to learn from.
practice.step5: Results tracks every attempt so you can watch your score improve.
practice.tip: Retake mocks as often as you like — repetition is how past-paper practice pays off.

papers.title: Past papers by year and stream
papers.summary: National past papers are organized by exam year (E.C.), stream and subject — practice or simulate the real sitting.
papers.step1: Open Exam prep and use the filters: grade, subject, year (E.C.), stream (natural/social) and paper type.
papers.step2: Practice sets show the answer and explanation immediately after each submission — use them to learn.
papers.step3: Mock exams run like the real thing: a timer, shuffled questions, and results only at the end.
papers.step4: Your best score is saved per paper — retake mocks until the score holds under exam conditions.
papers.tip: Study in passes: practice a year's paper first, then re-sit it as a mock a week later.

tutoring.title: Tutoring (for tutors)
tutoring.tagline: Your tutor profile, monthly escrow and earnings

becomeTutor.title: Become a verified tutor
becomeTutor.summary: Apply once; Temari.et staff verify your identity and documents before your profile goes live in the public directory.
becomeTutor.step1: Open Tutoring → Become a tutor (or temari.et/tutors → Apply now).
becomeTutor.step2: Fill your profile: headline, about, how you teach (online, in person or both), city and languages.
becomeTutor.step3: Add your subjects with the grades you cover, and set your hourly rate in ETB.
becomeTutor.step4: Enter your Fayda ID number and upload your credentials — teachers can attach documents straight from their school employee file.
becomeTutor.step5: Submit. You will be notified when the review is done; approved profiles appear in the directory immediately.
becomeTutor.tip: A clear headline, a real photo and a fair rate win far more requests than a long bio.

monthlyEscrow.title: How the monthly escrow works
monthlyEscrow.summary: Families prepay each Ethiopian month to Temari.et. You teach, they confirm, and the month is released to your wallet minus the platform commission.
monthlyEscrow.step1: When you accept a request, the engagement is created and the first month is billed to the family.
monthlyEscrow.step2: Sessions stay locked until the family pays — never teach an unpaid month.
monthlyEscrow.step3: During the month, log each session after it happens; the family has 72 hours to confirm (silence auto-confirms).
monthlyEscrow.step4: After the month ends, Temari.et releases confirmed hours × your rate − commission to your wallet.
monthlyEscrow.step5: Hours that were paid but not taught roll into the next month as credit for the family.
monthlyEscrow.tip: Only CONFIRMED sessions are paid — log sessions promptly so the confirmation clock starts.

runSessions.title: Schedule, teach and log sessions
runSessions.summary: Sessions live inside the paid month: schedule ahead, teach (online rooms are created for you), then mark as given.
runSessions.step1: Open the engagement and press Schedule session — pick date, time and duration.
runSessions.step2: Online engagements get a meeting room link automatically; share happens in-app, both sides see Join meeting.
runSessions.step3: After the lesson, press Mark as given (adjust the real duration if it differed).
runSessions.step4: The family confirms or raises an issue; disputed sessions are reviewed by Temari.et and freeze only that session's value.
runSessions.step5: Cancel sessions that will not happen — canceled sessions are never billed.
runSessions.tip: Use the chat thread for rescheduling — it keeps the agreement on record.

earningsPayouts.title: Wallet, payouts and your account
earningsPayouts.summary: Released months land in your Temari.et wallet; withdraw to your bank account or Telebirr wallet.
earningsPayouts.step1: Open Tutoring → Earnings to see your balance, wallet history and past payouts.
earningsPayouts.step2: Save your payout account first: bank or Telebirr, account number and the exact account holder name.
earningsPayouts.step3: Press Request payout and enter the amount (minimum 50 ETB, up to your balance).
earningsPayouts.step4: Temari.et approves and sends the money — you are notified when it is paid.
earningsPayouts.step5: If a transfer fails, the amount returns to your wallet automatically.
earningsPayouts.tip: One payout can be in progress at a time — request once, not repeatedly.

boostProfile.title: Feature your profile
boostProfile.summary: Featured tutors rank at the top of the directory with a badge — more views, more requests.
boostProfile.step1: Open Tutoring → Earnings → Boost profile and pick a plan (1 week or 30 days).
boostProfile.step2: Pay with any available method; the boost activates the moment payment confirms.
boostProfile.step3: Buying again extends the current boost — time never overlaps or resets.
boostProfile.tip: Boosts work best right after you improve your profile and rate.

marketplaceAdmin.title: Tutoring marketplace (operators)
marketplaceAdmin.tagline: Vet tutors, control the escrow money, run payouts

reviewTutors.title: Review tutor applications
reviewTutors.summary: Every tutor is vetted by Temari.et before going live: identity (Fayda), credentials and a sane profile.
reviewTutors.step1: Open Tutor review and filter the queue by Under review.
reviewTutors.step2: Open the application: read the profile, open every document, and check the Fayda number against the uploaded ID scan.
reviewTutors.step3: Approve to publish the profile in the public directory (a public link is created).
reviewTutors.step4: Decline with a clear reason — the applicant can fix it and resubmit.
reviewTutors.step5: Suspend approved tutors on serious reports; reinstate when resolved.
reviewTutors.tip: Unreadable document scans are the most common decline reason — say exactly which file to re-upload.

moneyConsole.title: Run the escrow money console
moneyConsole.summary: Every family payment is held by Temari.et until the month is taught and confirmed. You control releases, refunds and the payout desk.
moneyConsole.step1: Open Marketplace money — the header shows held escrow, releasable months, commission collected and totals released.
moneyConsole.step2: The Ready to release filter lists finished months with every session decided — release them to credit the tutor's wallet.
moneyConsole.step3: A release computes confirmed hours × rate − commission; unfulfilled value carries to the family's next month automatically.
moneyConsole.step4: Refund a funded month only when an engagement ends early; record how the money was returned in the note.
moneyConsole.step5: On the Payout desk: approve (reserves the funds), then send via Chapa or mark as manually paid.
moneyConsole.tip: Resolve disputed sessions first — a month with open disputes cannot be released.

gatewaysSetup.title: Configure payment gateways
gatewaysSetup.summary: The gateway matrix decides which providers are live and what each may collect. Credentials live in server config only.
gatewaysSetup.step1: Open Payment gateways — each gateway shows whether its credentials are configured on the server.
gatewaysSetup.step2: Enable a gateway and tick the purposes it may collect (tutoring, AI subscription, boosts, School Plan).
gatewaysSetup.step3: Set the marketplace knobs: commission percent, boost prices, and auto-release days (empty = manual releases).
gatewaysSetup.step4: Save — checkout options update instantly for every payer.
gatewaysSetup.tip: School fees never flow through these gateways — they collect Temari.et's own revenue only.

temariAi.title: Temari AI
temariAi.tagline: Your AI assistant for studying, parenting and running the school

chat.title: Chat with Temari AI
chat.summary: Temari AI is a private chat assistant that answers from your real school data — your role decides what it can see and do.
chat.step1: Open Temari AI from the sidebar (or the bottom bar on mobile). Your conversations are private — nobody else can read them.
chat.step2: Type your question straight into the message box — it is ready as soon as the page opens. Your workspace decides which assistant answers: from a school workspace you get your school assistant, and from the family side (My children / My learning) your family assistant — nothing to pick.
chat.step3: Ask in English, Amharic or Afan Oromo. Every number in an answer comes from the school's records, never guessed.
chat.step4: Attach photos or files — homework photos, PDFs, Word, Excel or PowerPoint — and ask about them. You can also paste a screenshot or drag a file straight into the message box.
chat.step5: Your past chats live in the list beside the conversation (on the phone, tap the clock button to open them). Pin, rename or delete chats there, and rate answers with 👍/👎 to help improve the assistant.
chat.tip: The assistant refuses politely when your account cannot see something (for example fees without the fee permission) — those rules are the same as the rest of the app.

examBuilder.title: Build a whole exam with AI
examBuilder.summary: Teachers can create a complete draft exam from a chat — the assistant asks for the class, chapter and shape with tap-to-answer buttons, drafts the questions and files everything for your review.
examBuilder.step1: Open Exams and press "Create with AI" (or open Temari AI and write, for example, "Create a 10-question exam for Grade 1 Mathematics, Chapter 1").
examBuilder.step2: Answer the assistant's short questions by tapping the buttons: which of your classes sits the paper, what it covers, how many questions, which types — multiple choice, true/false, short answer, matching, or a reading passage with its own sub-questions — and difficulty. You can always type your own answer instead — and the buttons keep working even after a page refresh.
examBuilder.step3: The assistant shows the full paper in the chat first — every question with its answer marked. Ask for changes in plain words ("make question 3 harder", "add two true/false").
examBuilder.step4: Approve, and it creates everything at once: the questions land as drafts in a question bank and a draft exam is assembled for your sections, with a link straight to it.
examBuilder.step5: Open the exam in the studio, review the questions, adjust points or timing, and publish it yourself — nothing the AI makes is ever visible to students until you publish.
examBuilder.tip: Already have a question bank? Ask the assistant to build the exam from it — it can mix your existing questions with newly drafted ones.

sendMessages.title: Draft and send messages with AI
sendMessages.summary: Temari AI can write a message with you — to a student's family, a colleague or an announcement channel — and hand it to Messages. You always review it and press Send yourself.
sendMessages.step1: Tell the assistant who the message is for and what it should say — for example "Write a message to Eyob's parents about his progress in Mathematics".
sendMessages.step2: The assistant checks who you are allowed to message — a teacher reaches only the families of their own classes — and asks if anything is unclear.
sendMessages.step3: Review the draft in the chat and ask for changes in plain words: shorter, warmer, English and Amharic together — until it reads right.
sendMessages.step4: When it is ready, a send card appears showing the recipient and the text. You can still edit the text on the card with the pencil button.
sendMessages.step5: Press Send. The message travels through Messages under the school's normal rules — if your school reviews staff messages to families first, the card shows "Awaiting approval". Open the conversation any time from the card.
sendMessages.tip: Parents can use this too: ask the assistant to write to your child's teacher or the school office, in the language you prefer.

familyAi.title: For students and parents
familyAi.summary: Students get a personal tutor grounded in their own results; parents can ask about their child in plain language.
familyAi.step1: Students: ask for explanations, study plans, or "why did I lose marks?" — the tutor reads your results and past quiz attempts and recommends matching exam-prep papers.
familyAi.step2: Parents: ask "How is my child doing?" in Amharic or any language — marks, attendance, homework and fees, gated by your guardian permissions.
familyAi.step3: During a live exam the tutor will not answer exam questions — it helps you study before and reviews mistakes after results are released.
familyAi.step4: With several children, name the child you are asking about, or start the question with their first name.
familyAi.tip: The free tier gives a few messages per day. The Temari AI subscription unlocks full daily use for the whole family account.

schoolAi.title: For teachers and school leaders
schoolAi.summary: Teachers get a copilot over their own classes; directors and principals get school analytics in plain questions.
schoolAi.step1: Teachers: analyze your classes, find struggling students, draft quiz questions into your question banks (always as drafts you review), and draft report-card comments or parent messages.
schoolAi.step2: Look for the ✨ AI assist button inside the question-bank studio and lesson planner — it generates drafts right where you work.
schoolAi.step3: Leaders: ask "which subject is weakest?", "who is at risk?", "compare sections" — answers come from frozen term results and attendance records with practical recommendations.
schoolAi.step4: A weekly AI briefing lands in your notifications with the students who need attention — open Temari AI to dig deeper.
schoolAi.tip: School AI is part of the School Plan. Without it, staff get a small daily teaser — ask your administrator about the plan.

subscription.title: Plans and payment
subscription.summary: Family AI is a personal subscription paid online; School AI comes with the school's School Plan.
subscription.step1: Students and parents subscribe in the app — when you hit the daily free limit, tap "Get Temari AI".
subscription.step2: Pay with Chapa, Telebirr or CBE Birr. The subscription starts immediately after payment and runs 30 days.
subscription.step3: Renewing early never loses days — new days are added to the end of your current subscription.
subscription.step4: School AI (leadership analytics + teacher copilot) is enabled for the whole school by Temari.et when the school joins the School Plan.
subscription.tip: This subscription is Temari's own service — it is separate from school fees, which always go directly to your school.
